title.zh: 卷六十九 列傳第五十九 沈炯 虞荔 傅縡 顧野王 姚察
title.en: Volume 69 Biographies 59: Shen Jiong, Yu Li, Fu Zai, Prince of Guye, Yao Chao
title.raw: 卷六十九 列傳第五十九 沈炯 虞荔 傅縡 顧野王 姚察 Volume 69 Biographies 59: Shen Jiong, Yu Li, Fu Zai, Prince of Guye, Yao Chao

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十九

translations.literal: Biographies number fifty-nine
translations.idiomatic: the 59th year of Biography

sentences.zh: 沈炯虞荔傅縡顧野王姚察

translations.literal: Shen Jiong, Yu Li, Fu Zai, Gu Yewang, Yao Chao
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jiong, Yu Li, Fu Zai, Gu Yewang, and Yao Chao

sentences.zh: 沈炯字初明，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Jiong, courtesy name Chuming, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jiong, whose courtesy name was Chuming, came from Wukang in Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖瑀，梁尋陽太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yu was Administrator of Xunyang under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu had served as Administrator of Xunyang under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 父續，王府記室參軍。

translations.literal: His father Xu was Registrar on a princely staff.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xu held the post of Registrar on a prince's staff.

sentences.zh: 炯少有俊才，為當時所重。

translations.literal: Jiong in youth had outstanding talent and was esteemed by his age.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Jiong showed remarkable talent and won the respect of his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 仕梁為尚書左戶侍郎、吳令。

translations.literal: He served Liang as Left Household Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Magistrate of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liang he rose to Left Household Vice Minister in the Secretariat and Magistrate of Wu.

sentences.zh: 侯景之難，吳郡太守袁君正入援建鄴，以炯監郡。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Hou Jing, Wu commandery Administrator Yuan Junzheng went to aid Jiankang and made Jiong overseer of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Yuan Junzheng, Administrator of Wu commandery, marched to relieve Jiankang and left Jiong in charge of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 台城陷，景將宋子仙據吳興，使召炯，方委以書記，炯辭以疾，子仙怒，命斬之。

translations.literal: When the Terrace City fell, Jing's general Song Zixian held Wuxing and summoned Jiong; just as he was to entrust him with secretarial duties, Jiong pleaded illness; Zixian was angry and ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: After the Terrace City fell, Hou Jing's general Song Zixian seized Wuxing and summoned Jiong to serve as his secretary. Jiong pleaded illness; Zixian flew into a rage and ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 炯解衣將就戮，礙于路間桑樹，乃更牽往他所，或救之，僅而獲免。

translations.literal: Jiong removed his robe to await execution; blocked by mulberry trees along the road, they dragged him elsewhere; someone rescued him, and he barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong stripped for the block, but mulberry trees along the road impeded the blow, so his guards hauled him elsewhere. Someone intervened, and he barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 子仙愛其才，終逼之令掌書記。

translations.literal: Zixian prized his talent and in the end compelled him to take charge of secretarial work.
translations.idiomatic: Zixian admired his gifts and eventually forced him to serve as secretary after all.

sentences.zh: 及子仙敗，王僧辯素聞其名，軍中購得之，酬所獲者錢十萬，自是羽檄軍書，皆出於炯。

translations.literal: When Zixian was defeated, Wang Sengbian had long heard his name; the army bought him out and rewarded the finder with a hundred thousand cash; thereafter all urgent dispatches and military documents came from Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: After Zixian's defeat, Wang Sengbian, who had long known Jiong's reputation, ransomed him from the ranks for a reward of a hundred thousand cash. From then on every urgent dispatch and military document issued from Sengbian's camp bore Jiong's hand.

sentences.zh: 及簡文遇害，四方嶽牧上表勸進，僧辯令炯製錶，當時莫有逮者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jianwen was killed, regional governors everywhere submitted memorials urging advancement; Sengbian had Jiong draft the memorial, and none of the time could match it.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Jianwen was murdered, governors throughout the realm submitted memorials urging the throne onward. Sengbian charged Jiong with drafting them, and none of his contemporaries could rival his prose.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝南下，與僧辯會白茅灣，登壇設盟，炯為其文。

translations.literal: Chen Wudi marched south; he and Sengbian met at Baimao Bay, ascended the altar and set the covenant; Jiong composed its text.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi marched south and met Sengbian at Baimao Bay, they ascended the altar to swear their alliance, and Jiong wrote the covenant.

sentences.zh: 及景東奔，至吳郡，獲炯妻虞氏及子行簡，並殺之，炯弟攜其母逃免。

translations.literal: When Jing fled east and reached Wu commandery, he seized Jiong's wife Lady Yu and son Xingjian and killed them both; Jiong's younger brother fled with their mother and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: As Hou Jing fled eastward into Wu commandery, he seized Jiong's wife Lady Yu and their son Xingjian and put them to death. Jiong's younger brother escaped with their mother.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，梁元帝湣其妻子嬰戮，特封原鄉侯。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Liang Emperor Yuan pitied that his wife and son had met violent death and specially enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yuanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing's defeat, Emperor Yuan of Liang mourned the slaughter of Jiong's wife and son and specially enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yuanxiang.

sentences.zh: 僧辯為司徒，以炯為從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Sengbian became Minister of Works, he made Jiong Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengbian was appointed Minister of Works, he named Jiong Attendant Gentleman on his staff.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝徵為給事黃門侍郎，領尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Liang Emperor Yuan summoned him as Yellow Gate Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrent Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan summoned him to the post of Yellow Gate Attendant-in-Ordinary with concurrent duty as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 魏克荊州，被虜，甚見禮遇，授儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Wei took Jingzhou, he was captured and greatly honored, appointed Commissioner with the Protocol of Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Wei conquered Jingzhou he was taken captive but treated with great honor and granted the rank of Commissioner with the Protocol of Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 以母在東，恒思歸國，恐以文才被留，閉門卻掃，無所交接。

translations.literal: Because his mother was in the east, he constantly thought of returning home; fearing he would be kept for his literary talent, he shut his gate and swept away visitors, associating with no one.
translations.idiomatic: His mother remained in the east, and he longed constantly to return. Fearing the Wei would detain him for his literary gifts, he shut his gate to visitors and kept company with no one.

sentences.zh: 時有文章，隨即棄毀，不令流布。

translations.literal: Whenever he wrote, he at once discarded and destroyed it, not allowing it to circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he composed something, he destroyed it at once rather than let it circulate.

sentences.zh: 嘗獨行經漢武通天台，為表奏之，陳己思鄉之意。

translations.literal: Once walking alone past the Han Emperor Wu's Terrace of Communication with Heaven, he composed a memorial and submitted it, stating his longing for home.
translations.idiomatic: Once, walking alone past Emperor Wu of Han's Terrace of Communication with Heaven, he drafted a memorial there expressing his longing to return home.

sentences.zh: 曰：「臣聞橋山雖掩，鼎湖之灶可祠；

translations.literal: He said: "Your servant has heard that though Qiaoshan may conceal the body, the stove at Dinghu may still be worshipped;
translations.idiomatic: It read: "I have heard that though Mount Qiao may hide the sage's remains, the altar at Lake Ding may still receive offerings;

sentences.zh: 有魯遂荒，大庭之跡無泯。

translations.literal: though Youlu fell to waste, the traces at Great Court have not perished.
translations.idiomatic: though Youlu fell into ruin, the traces at the Great Court have not vanished.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下降德猗蘭，纂靈豐穀，漢道既登，神仙可望。

translations.literal: Bowingly: Your Majesty's virtue descended like orchids in shade, inheriting numinous power from abundant valleys; the Han Way has ascended, immortals may be hoped for.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's virtue spreads like orchids in the shade; you inherit a numinous legacy from a land of plenty. The Han way has reached its height, and immortality lies within reach.

sentences.zh: 射之罘於海浦，禮日觀而稱功，橫中流於汾河，指柏梁而高宴，何其甚樂，豈不然歟！

translations.literal: Shooting at Zhifu on the sea shore, performing rites at Mount Ri and proclaiming merit, crossing midstream on the Fen, pointing to Cypress Beam for lofty feasting—how very joyful, is it not so!
translations.idiomatic: You hunted at Zhifu by the sea, paid rites at Mount Ri and proclaimed your achievements, crossed the Fen midstream, and feasted high at Cypress Beam—what boundless joy, was it not so!

sentences.zh: 既而運屬上仙，道窮晏駕，甲帳珠簾，一朝零落，茂陵玉碗，遂出人間。

translations.literal: Then fate turned to the transcendent lord, the Way ended in the peaceful carriage; armored curtains and pearl blinds fell in a morning; the jade bowl of Maoling passed into the human world.
translations.idiomatic: Then fate turned toward the transcendent realm, the Way reached its end at the imperial deathbed; armored curtains and pearl blinds collapsed in a single morning, and the jade bowl of Maoling passed into mortal hands.

sentences.zh: 陵雲故基，與原田而膴膴，別風餘跡，帶陵阜而芒芒，羈旅縲臣，豈不落淚。

translations.literal: The old foundation of Lingyun, with open fields lush and wide; remaining traces of the departing wind, girdling hillocks in boundless haze—a captive wanderer in bonds, how could he not shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: The old foundations of Lingyun Terrace merge with broad fields stretching green and wide; lingering traces of departed glory wind through the mounds in endless haze. A captive wanderer in bonds—how could he not weep?

sentences.zh: 昔承明見厭，嚴助東歸，駟馬可乘，長卿西反，恭聞故實，竊有愚心。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Chenming grew wearisome, Yan Zhu returned east; four-horse carriages could be taken, Sima Xiangru came back from the west—I respectfully hear these old precedents and privately harbor a simple wish.
translations.idiomatic: In old times, when the Hall of Chenming grew tiresome, Yan Zhu returned east; a four-horse carriage awaited Sima Xiangru's journey west. I have heard these precedents with reverence and dare harbor a humble wish of my own.

sentences.zh: 黍稷非馨，敢望徼福。

translations.literal: Millet and millet are not fragrant; I dare not hope for stolen blessing.
translations.idiomatic: My humble offerings lack fragrance; I dare not hope for undeserved grace.

sentences.zh: 但雀台之吊，空愴魏君，雍丘之祠，未光夏後，瞻仰煙霞，伏增淒戀。」

translations.literal: Yet the lament at Sparrow Terrace only grieves the Wei lord in vain; the sacrifice at Yongqiu has not yet honored the Xia successor—gazing up at mist and rosy clouds, prostrate, my desolate longing grows."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the lament at Sparrow Terrace grieves the Wei lord to no avail, and the rites at Yongqiu have not yet honored the Xia heir. Gazing toward the mists and dawn light, I prostrate myself, and my desolate longing only deepens."

sentences.zh: 奏訖，其夜夢有宮禁之所，兵衛甚嚴，炯便以情事陳訴。

translations.literal: When the memorial was finished, that night he dreamed of a palace precinct with very strict guards; Jiong stated his circumstances in appeal.
translations.idiomatic: After he submitted the memorial, that night he dreamed of the palace precincts, heavily guarded. Jiong pleaded his case in the dream.

sentences.zh: 聞有人言：「甚不惜放卿還，幾時可至。」

translations.literal: He heard someone say: "We are quite willing to let you return—when can you arrive?"
translations.idiomatic: He heard a voice say, "We are quite willing to let you go home—when can you arrive?"

sentences.zh: 少日，便與王克等並獲東歸。

translations.literal: Before long, he and Wang Ke and others were all able to return east together.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was permitted to return east together with Wang Ke and the others.

sentences.zh: 曆司農卿，御史中丞。

translations.literal: He successively served as Minister of Agriculture and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Minister of Agriculture and as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝受禪，加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Chen Wudi received the abdication, Jiong was additionally made Regular Attendant of the Direct and Upright Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi accepted the abdication, Jiong was further appointed Regular Attendant of the Direct and Upright Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 表求歸養，詔不許。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting to return home to support his mother; the edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial asking to go home and care for his mother, but the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 文帝嗣位，又表求去，詔答曰：「當敕所由，相迎尊累，使卿公私無廢也。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he again memorialized to leave; the edict replied: "We shall order the authorities to welcome your honored kin, so that neither your public nor private duties need suffer."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Jiong again asked to resign. The edict answered: "We shall order the authorities to bring your honored kin here, so that neither your public service nor your family duties need suffer."

sentences.zh: 初，武帝嘗稱炯宜居王佐，軍國大政，多預謀謨。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wudi had said Jiong was fit to assist a king; in great military and state affairs he often took part in planning.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wudi had said that Jiong was fit to serve as a prince's chief aide, and he took part in planning most major military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 文帝又重其才，欲寵貴之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen also valued his talent and wished to honor and enrich him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen likewise prized his talent and wished to shower him with honors.

sentences.zh: 會王琳入寇大雷，留異擁據東境，帝欲使炯因是立功，乃解中丞，加明威將軍，遣還鄉里，收徒眾。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Lin invaded Dalei and Liu Yi held the eastern marches; the Emperor wished Jiong to win merit thereby, so removed him as Censor-in-Chief, added General of Illustrious Might, sent him back to his home district to gather followers.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lin invaded Dalei and Liu Yi held the eastern territories, the Emperor hoped Jiong would distinguish himself in the crisis. He relieved him of the censorate, made him General of Illustrious Might, and sent him home to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 以疾卒于吳中，贈侍中，諡恭子。

translations.literal: He died of illness in Wu and was posthumously made Palace Attendant, posthumous name Gongzi.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in Wu. Posthumously he was made Palace Attendant with the posthumous name Gongzi, "The Respectful."

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷行於世。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in twenty juan circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: A collection of his writings in twenty juan circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 虞荔字山披，會稽余姚人也。

translations.literal: Yu Li, courtesy name Shanpi, was a native of Yuyao in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Li, whose courtesy name was Shanpi, came from Yuyao in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖權，梁廷尉卿、永嘉太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Quan was Liang Minister of Justice and Administrator of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Quan had served the Liang as Minister of Justice and Administrator of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 父檢，平北始興王諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His father Jian was Staff Adviser to the Prince of Shixing, Pacifier of the North.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jian had been Staff Adviser to the Prince of Shixing, Pacifier of the North.

sentences.zh: 荔幼聰敏，有志操。

translations.literal: Li in youth was clever and keen, with purpose and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Li was quick-witted and possessed firm moral purpose.

sentences.zh: 年九歲，隨從伯闡候太常陸倕，倕問五經十事，荔對無遺失，倕甚異之。

translations.literal: At age nine, following his father's elder cousin Kan, he visited Grand Master of Ceremonies Lu Yan; Yan asked ten matters from the Five Classics; Li answered without omission; Yan was greatly struck.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he accompanied his father's elder cousin Kan on a visit to Lu Yan, Grand Master of Ceremonies. Yan posed ten questions drawn from the Five Classics; Li answered every one without fault, and Yan was astonished.

sentences.zh: 又嘗詣征士何胤，時太守衡陽王亦造之，胤言于王，王欲見荔，荔辭曰：「未有板刺，無容拜謁。」

translations.literal: He also once called on the recluse He Yin; at the time the Prince of Hengyang, then Administrator, also came to visit; Yin spoke to the prince; the prince wished to see Li; Li declined: "I have no visiting card—there is no occasion for an audience."
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he called on the recluse He Yin while the Prince of Hengyang, then serving as commandery administrator, was also visiting. Yin mentioned Li to the prince, who wished to receive him. Li declined: "I have no visiting card and am in no position to pay a formal call."

sentences.zh: 王以荔有高尚之志，雅相欽重，還郡，即辟為主簿，荔又辭以年小不就。

translations.literal: The prince, seeing Li's lofty resolve, greatly admired him; returning to his commandery, he at once summoned him as Chief Clerk; Li again declined on grounds of youth and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The prince admired Li's lofty character and held him in high esteem. Back in his commandery he immediately summoned Li as Chief Clerk, but Li again declined on grounds of youth.

sentences.zh: 及長，美風儀，博覽墳籍，善屬文。

translations.literal: When grown, he had fine bearing, broadly read the classics, and was skilled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he possessed striking presence, had read widely in the classics, and wrote with skill.

sentences.zh: 仕梁為西中郎法曹外兵參軍，兼丹陽詔獄正。

translations.literal: He served Liang as External Military Assistant in the Law Section of the Western Central Commandant's office, and concurrent Director of Danyang Imperial Prison.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liang he served as External Military Assistant in the Western Central Commandant's law office and concurrently as Director of the Danyang imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝於城西置士林館，荔乃制碑奏上，帝命勒之於館，仍用荔為士林學士。

translations.literal: Liang Emperor Wu established the Forest of Literati Hall west of the city; Li composed a stele inscription and submitted it; the Emperor ordered it carved at the hall and made Li a scholar of the Forest of Literati.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang founded the Forest of Literati Hall west of the capital. Li composed a stele inscription and submitted it; the Emperor ordered it carved at the hall and appointed Li a scholar there.

sentences.zh: 尋為司文郎，遷通直散騎侍郎，兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Lang of the Documents Office, promoted to Vice Director of the Direct and Upright Cavalry, and concurrent Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Lang of the Documents Office, then Vice Director of the Direct and Upright Cavalry with concurrent duty as Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 時左右之任，多參權軸，內外機務，互有帶掌，唯荔與顧協泊然靜退，居於西省，但以文史見知。

translations.literal: At the time those in attendance often shared in the hubs of power; inner and outer affairs were mutually held in overlapping charge; only Li and Gu Xie were tranquil and retiring, dwelling in the Western Secretariat, known only through letters and histories.
translations.idiomatic: At that time most court attendants meddled in the centers of power and jostled for overlapping control of civil and military affairs. Only Li and Gu Xie remained calm and withdrawn in the Western Secretariat, known solely for their literary and historical expertise.

sentences.zh: 尋領大著作。

translations.literal: Soon he headed the Grand Historiographer's office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took charge of the Grand Historiographer's office.

sentences.zh: 及侯景之亂，荔率親屬入台，除鎮西諮議參軍，舍人如故。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing's turmoil came, Li led kin into the Terrace City, was made Staff Adviser to the Pacifier of the West, and kept his drafter post.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion Li led his family into the Terrace City. He was appointed Staff Adviser to the Pacifier of the West while retaining his post as Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 台城陷，逃歸鄉里。

translations.literal: When the Terrace City fell, he fled home to his district.
translations.idiomatic: When the Terrace City fell, he fled home.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，元帝徵為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Yuan summoned him as Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing's defeat, Emperor Yuan summoned him as Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 貞陽侯僭位，授揚州別駕，並不就。

translations.literal: When the Marquis of Zhenyang usurped the throne, he was given Yangzhou Vice Administrator; he accepted neither post.
translations.idiomatic: When the Marquis of Zhenyang seized the throne, Li was offered the post of Yangzhou Vice Administrator, but he accepted neither appointment.

sentences.zh: 張彪之據會稽，荔時在焉。

translations.literal: When Zhang Biao held Kuaiji, Li was there at the time.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Biao seized Kuaiji, Li happened to be there.

sentences.zh: 及文帝平彪，武帝及文帝並書招之，迫切不得已，乃應命至都，而武帝崩，文帝嗣位，除太子中庶子，仍侍太子讀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen pacified Biao, both Wudi and Wen wrote to summon him; pressed hard with no escape, he answered the summons to the capital; Wudi died; Wen succeeded; Li was made Crown Prince Attendant, still attending the crown prince's studies.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen defeated Biao, both Wudi and Wen wrote urging him to court. Unable to refuse their repeated summons, he went to the capital. Wudi died before his arrival; Wen succeeded and appointed him Crown Prince Attendant while keeping him as tutor to the heir.

sentences.zh: 尋領大著作。

translations.literal: Soon he again headed the Grand Historiographer's office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resumed charge of the Grand Historiographer's office.

sentences.zh: 初，荔母隨荔入台，卒於台內，尋而城陷，情禮不申，由是終身蔬食布衣，不聽音樂。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li's mother had entered the Terrace with him and died within it; soon the city fell and ritual feeling could not be expressed; from this he for life ate vegetables and wore plain cloth, and did not listen to music.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li's mother had accompanied him into the Terrace City and died there. The city soon fell before mourning rites could be observed. From then on he ate only vegetables, wore plain cloth, and refused all music for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 雖任遇隆重，而居止儉素，淡然無營。

translations.literal: Though his appointments were weighty, his dwelling was frugal and plain, detached without scheming.
translations.idiomatic: Though his appointments were exalted, he lived frugally and sought nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 文帝深器之，常引在左右，朝夕顧訪。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen greatly treasured him, often keeping him at his side, attending to him morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen valued him deeply, kept him constantly at his side, and sought his counsel morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 荔性沈密，少言論，凡所獻替，莫有見其際者。

translations.literal: Li's nature was deep and close; he spoke little; whatever he offered or withdrew, none saw its inner workings.
translations.idiomatic: Li was reserved and discreet, spoke little, and none could tell when he had offered counsel behind the scenes.

sentences.zh: 第二弟寄，寓於閩中，依陳寶應，荔每言之輒流涕。

translations.literal: His second younger brother Ji was staying in Min, relying on Chen Baoying; whenever Li spoke of it he would weep.
translations.idiomatic: His second younger brother Ji was living in Min under Chen Baoying's protection, and Li wept whenever he spoke of him.

sentences.zh: 文帝哀而謂曰：「我亦有弟在遠，此情甚切，他人豈知。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen pitied him and said: "I too have a brother far away; this feeling is very keen—how could others know?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was moved and said, "I too have a brother far away. This longing cuts deep—who else could understand it?"

sentences.zh: 乃敕寶應求寄，寶應終不遣。

translations.literal: He then ordered Baoying to send Ji back; Baoying in the end would not release him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Baoying to send Ji back, but Baoying never released him.

sentences.zh: 荔因以感疾，帝欲數往臨視，令將家口入省。

translations.literal: Li thereby fell ill with grief; the Emperor wished to visit him often and ordered his household brought into the palace offices.
translations.idiomatic: Li fell ill from grief. The Emperor wished to visit him often and ordered his household brought into the palace compound.

sentences.zh: 荔以禁中非私居之所，乞停城外，帝不許，乃令住蘭台。

translations.literal: Li held that the forbidden precinct was no place for private dwelling and begged to stay outside the walls; the Emperor did not permit it and had him lodge at the Orchid Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Li protested that the palace was no private home and asked to stay outside the walls. The Emperor refused and had him lodge at the Orchid Terrace instead.

sentences.zh: 乘輿再三臨問，手敕中使相望於道。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage visited him again and again; handwritten edicts and palace envoys lined the road one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor visited him repeatedly, and handwritten edicts and palace envoys crowded the road in succession.

sentences.zh: 又以蔬食積久，非羸疾所堪，乃敕曰：「卿年事已多，氣力稍減，方欲仗委，良須克壯。

translations.literal: Also, because vegetable fare over long time was not what a wasting illness could bear, he issued an edict: "Your years are already many, your strength somewhat reduced; we are just about to rely on you—you truly must recover robustness.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that prolonged abstinence from meat was too much for his frail body, the Emperor wrote: "You are advanced in years and your strength has waned. We mean to rely on you still—you must regain your vigor.

sentences.zh: 今給卿魚肉，不得固從所執。」

translations.literal: Now we give you fish and meat; you must not stubbornly follow what you have held to."
translations.idiomatic: We now supply you with fish and meat. You must not cling stubbornly to your vow."

sentences.zh: 荔終不從。

translations.literal: Li in the end did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Li still refused.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈侍中，諡曰德子。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Palace Attendant; posthumous name Dezi.
translations.idiomatic: He died. Posthumously he was made Palace Attendant with the posthumous name Dezi, "The Virtuous."

sentences.zh: 及喪柩還鄉里，上親出臨送，當時榮之。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned to his home district, the sovereign personally went out to see him off; the age counted it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: When his coffin returned home, the Emperor went out in person to escort it—a mark of honor that his contemporaries envied.

sentences.zh: 子世基、世南，並少知名。

translations.literal: His sons Shiji and Shinan were both known from youth.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Shiji and Shinan were both celebrated from an early age.

sentences.zh: 寄字次安，少聰敏。

translations.literal: Ji, courtesy name Ci'an, was clever in youth.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, whose courtesy name was Ci'an, was quick-witted as a boy.

sentences.zh: 年數歲，客有造其父，遇寄於門，嘲曰：「郎子姓虞，必當無智。」

translations.literal: At several years old, a guest came to visit his father and met Ji at the gate, mocking: "Young master surnamed Yu must surely lack wisdom."
translations.idiomatic: When he was only a few years old, a visitor called on his father and met Ji at the gate. The man jested, "A lad surnamed Yu must surely lack wit."

sentences.zh: 寄應聲曰：「文字不辨，豈得非愚！」

translations.literal: Ji answered on the spot: "If you cannot distinguish written characters, how are you not foolish!"
translations.idiomatic: Ji shot back, "If you cannot tell one character from another, who is the fool here?"

sentences.zh: 客大慚。

translations.literal: The guest was greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The guest was deeply embarrassed.

sentences.zh: 入謂其父：「此子非常人，文舉之對，不是過也。」

translations.literal: Entering, he told the father: "This child is no ordinary person; Kong Wenju's retort was no better."
translations.idiomatic: Inside he told Ji's father, "This boy is no ordinary child. His retort rivals Kong Rong's famous answer."

sentences.zh: 及長，好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: When grown, he loved learning and was skilled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he loved learning and wrote with skill.

sentences.zh: 性沖靜，有棲遁志。

translations.literal: His nature was mild and still; he had the resolve to dwell in seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: He was gentle and withdrawn by nature and aspired to a life of seclusion.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉秀才，對策高第。

translations.literal: At weak cap he was recommended as Cultivated Talent and ranked high in the policy response.
translations.idiomatic: At his coming of age he was recommended as Cultivated Talent and placed at the top of the policy examination.

sentences.zh: 起家梁宣城王國左常侍。

translations.literal: He began his career as Left Regular Attendant in the Liang Prince of Xuancheng's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Left Regular Attendant in the establishment of the Liang Prince of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 大同中，嘗驟雨，殿前往往有雜色寶珠，梁武觀之，甚有喜色，寄因上瑞雨頌。

translations.literal: In the Datong era, once during a sudden rain, before the hall there often appeared multicolored precious pearls; Liang Wu viewed them with great pleasure; Ji thereupon submitted an Ode on Auspicious Rain.
translations.idiomatic: During the Datong era a sudden rain once left multicolored pearls scattered before the hall. Emperor Wu looked on with delight, and Ji submitted an Ode on the Auspicious Rain.

sentences.zh: 帝謂寄兄荔曰：「此頌典裁清拔，卿之士龍也，將如何擢用？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Ji's elder brother Li: "This ode's style is clear and elevated; he is your Shi Long—how shall we promote and employ him?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Ji's elder brother Li, "This ode is elegant and elevated. He is your Lu Ji—how shall we promote him?"

sentences.zh: 寄聞之歎曰：「美盛德之形容，以申擊壤之情耳，吾豈買名求仕者乎？」

translations.literal: When Ji heard, he sighed: "To praise the sage virtue's likeness and express the feeling of beating clods—that is all; am I one who buys a name to seek office?"
translations.idiomatic: When Ji heard this he sighed. "I only meant to praise the Emperor's virtue and voice the people's joy. Am I the sort to trade on a name for office?"

sentences.zh: 乃閉門稱疾，唯以書籍自娛。

translations.literal: He then shut his gate and claimed illness, amusing himself only with books.
translations.idiomatic: He shut his gate, pleaded illness, and amused himself with books alone.

sentences.zh: 岳陽王察為會稽太守，寄為中記室，領郡五官掾。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yueyang Cha was Administrator of Kuaiji, Ji was Central Recorder and concurrent Commandery Five-Officials Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yueyang, Cha, became Administrator of Kuaiji, Ji served as Central Recorder with concurrent duty as Commandery Five-Officials Assistant.

sentences.zh: 在職簡略煩苛，務存大體，曹局之內，終日寂然。

translations.literal: In office he simplified what was tedious and exacting, keeping to the great pattern; within the bureau all day was silence.
translations.idiomatic: In office he cut through petty bureaucracy and kept to essentials. His bureau was silent all day long.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，寄隨兄荔入台，及城陷，遁還鄉里。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Ji followed his elder brother Li into the Terrace City; when the city fell he escaped back to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Ji followed his elder brother Li into the Terrace City. When the city fell he escaped back to his home district.

sentences.zh: 張彪往臨川，強寄俱行。

translations.literal: When Zhang Biao went to Linchuan he forced Ji to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Biao went to Linchuan he forced Ji to go with him.

sentences.zh: 寄與彪將鄭瑋同舟而載，瑋嘗忤彪意，乃劫寄奔晉安。

translations.literal: Ji traveled in the same boat as Biao's general Zheng Wei; Wei had once offended Biao, so he abducted Ji and fled to Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ji shared a boat with Biao's general Zheng Wei, who had once offended Biao; Wei therefore abducted Ji and fled to Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 時陳寶應據有閩中，得寄甚喜。

translations.literal: At the time Chen Baoying held Minzhong and was greatly pleased to gain Ji.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Chen Baoying held Minzhong and was delighted to gain Ji.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝平侯景，寄勸令自結，寶應從之，乃遣使歸誠。

translations.literal: When Chen Wudi pacified Hou Jing, Ji urged Baoying to bind himself to him; Baoying followed and sent an envoy to offer allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi pacified Hou Jing, Ji urged Baoying to bind himself to him. Baoying followed and sent an envoy to offer allegiance.

sentences.zh: 承聖元年，除中書侍郎，寶應愛其才，托以道阻不遣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chengsheng he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat; Baoying admired his talent and, claiming the roads were blocked, did not send him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chengsheng he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat. Baoying admired his talent and, claiming the roads were blocked, did not send him.

sentences.zh: 每欲引寄為僚屬，委以文翰，寄固辭獲免。

translations.literal: Whenever Baoying tried to draw Ji in as a subordinate and entrust writings to him, Ji firmly declined and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Baoying tried to bring Ji in as a subordinate and entrust writings to him, Ji firmly declined and was spared.

sentences.zh: 及寶應結昏留異，潛有逆謀，寄微知其意，言說之際，每陳逆順之理，微以諷諫。

translations.literal: When Baoying allied by marriage with Liu Yi and secretly harbored rebellious designs, Ji faintly knew his intent; in conversation he often set forth the logic of rebellion and obedience, subtly admonishing.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoying allied with Liu Yi by marriage and secretly plotted rebellion, Ji sensed his intent. In conversation he would explain the difference between loyalty and treason, hinting at admonition.

sentences.zh: 寶應輒引說他事以拒之。

translations.literal: Baoying would always turn to other topics to refuse him.
translations.idiomatic: Baoying always changed the subject to avoid him.

sentences.zh: 又嘗令左右讀漢書，臥而聽之，至蒯通說韓信曰：「相君之背，貴不可言」，寶應蹶然起曰：「可謂智士。」

translations.literal: He also once had attendants read the Book of Han while he lay listening; when it came to Kuai Tong telling Han Xin, "The back of my lord is noble beyond words," Baoying started up and said: "He may be called a wise man."
translations.idiomatic: Once he had an attendant read the Book of Han while he lay listening. At the passage where Kuai Tong tells Han Xin, "The back of my lord is noble beyond words," Baoying sat bolt upright and exclaimed, "Now there was a wise man!"

sentences.zh: 寄正色曰：「覆酈驕韓，未足稱智，豈若班彪王命識所歸乎？」

translations.literal: Ji with stern countenance said: "Overturning Li, arrogant toward Han—that is not enough to be called wisdom; how does it compare to Ban Biao's 'Kingly Mandate,' knowing where allegiance lies?"
translations.idiomatic: Ji said sternly, "Overthrowing Li and defying Han hardly counts as wisdom. How does that compare with Ban Biao's 'Kingly Mandate,' which knew where true allegiance lay?"

sentences.zh: 寄知寶應不可諫，慮禍及己，乃為居士服以拒絕之。

translations.literal: Ji knew Baoying could not be admonished and feared disaster reaching himself; he therefore wore lay Buddhist robes to refuse him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Baoying could not be persuaded and fearing he would be implicated, Ji put on lay Buddhist robes to keep his distance.

sentences.zh: 常居東山寺，偽稱腳疾，不復起。

translations.literal: He constantly dwelt at East Mountain Temple, falsely claiming foot ailment, and no longer rose.
translations.idiomatic: He took up residence at East Mountain Temple, feigned a foot ailment, and would not rise again.

sentences.zh: 寶應以為假託，遣人燒寄所臥屋，寄安臥不動。

translations.literal: Baoying thought it feigned and sent men to burn the house where Ji slept; Ji lay at ease without moving.
translations.idiomatic: Baoying assumed he was feigning illness and sent men to burn the house where Ji lay. Ji remained still and did not stir.

sentences.zh: 親近將扶寄出，寄曰：「吾命有所懸，避欲安往？」

translations.literal: Close attendants were about to help Ji out; Ji said: "My fate is still suspended—where would fleeing take me?"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants tried to help him out. Ji said, "My fate still hangs in the balance—where would fleeing take me?"

sentences.zh: 所縱火者，旋自救之。

translations.literal: Those who had set the fire soon themselves rescued him.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had set the fire soon put it out themselves.

sentences.zh: 寶應自此方信之。

translations.literal: From this Baoying finally believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Baoying believe that his illness was genuine.

sentences.zh: 及留異稱兵，寶應資其部曲，寄乃因書極諫曰：

translations.literal: When Liu Yi raised troops, Baoying supplied his forces; Ji then by letter remonstrated to the utmost, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yi took up arms, Baoying supplied his troops. Ji sent him a letter of the strongest remonstrance, which read:

sentences.zh: 東山居士虞寄致書于明將軍使君節下：寄流離艱故，飄寓貴鄉，將軍待以上賓之禮，申以國士之眷，意氣所感，何日忘之。

translations.literal: East Mountain Recluse Yu Ji sends this letter to the Illustrious General, Lord Envoy, beneath your banner: Ji, adrift through hardship and bereavement, lodged in your noble district; the General treated me with the rites due a chief guest and extended the affection owed a national champion—the feeling stirred between us, what day could I forget it?
translations.idiomatic: East Mountain Recluse Yu Ji to the Illustrious General, Lord Envoy: I have been adrift through hardship and loss and have found shelter in your domain. You received me with the honors due a chief guest and treated me with the affection owed a true champion of the state. The bond between us is something I could never forget.

sentences.zh: 而寄沈痼彌留，愒陰將盡，常恐卒填溝壑，涓塵莫報，是以敢布腹心，冒陳丹款，願將軍留須臾之慮，少思察之，則冥目之日，所懷畢矣。

translations.literal: Yet Ji's deep illness lingers on, the setting sun nearly spent; I constantly fear I may suddenly fill a ditch or gully and repay not even a drop of dust; therefore I dare lay bare my inmost heart and risk presenting my loyal sincerity, wishing the General would pause a moment's thought and reflect a little—then on the day my eyes close, what I hold in mind will be complete.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my illness grows grave and my days are nearly spent. I fear I may die at any moment without repaying even the smallest part of your kindness. I therefore dare lay bare my inmost heart and offer my loyal counsel. I beg you to pause for a moment and consider what I say. Then, when I close my eyes, I shall have nothing left unsaid.

sentences.zh: 夫安危之兆，禍福之機，匪獨天時，亦由人事。

translations.literal: Now the omens of safety and danger, the hinges of fortune and calamity, depend not on heaven's seasons alone but also on human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The signs of safety and danger, the turning points of fortune and ruin, depend not on heaven alone but on human conduct as well.

sentences.zh: 失之毫釐，差以千里。

translations.literal: Miss by a hair's breadth and err by a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: A slip of a hair's breadth can lead to an error of a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 是以明智之士，據重位而不傾，執大節而不失，豈惑於浮辭哉。

translations.literal: Therefore the wise man, holding a weighty post, does not topple; grasping great integrity, does not lose it—how could he be deluded by floating words?
translations.idiomatic: That is why the wise man holds high office without falling and keeps to great principle without wavering. How could he be swayed by empty rhetoric?

sentences.zh: 將軍文武兼資，英威動俗，往因多難，仗劍興師，援旗誓眾，抗威千里。

translations.literal: The General combines civil and martial gifts; heroic authority moves the age; in former days, amid many hardships, you took sword in hand and raised armies, lifted the banner and swore the host, and displayed might for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: You combine civil and martial gifts, and your heroic authority moves the age. In former days, amid many hardships, you took sword in hand, raised armies, lifted the banner to swear your troops, and displayed your might for a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 豈不以四郊多壘，共謀王室，匡時報主，甯國庇人乎。

translations.literal: Was it not because the four suburbs were full of ramparts, to plan together for the royal house, to rectify the age and repay the lord, to settle the state and shelter the people?
translations.idiomatic: Was that not because the realm was beset on every side, so that you might join in restoring the royal house, set the age aright, repay your sovereign, and bring peace to the state and shelter to the people?

sentences.zh: 此所以五尺童子，皆願荷戟而隨將軍者也。

translations.literal: This is why even a five-foot child wished to shoulder a halberd and follow the General.
translations.idiomatic: That is why even children wished to shoulder arms and follow you.

sentences.zh: 及高祖武皇帝肇基草昧，初濟艱難，于時天下沸騰，人無定主，豺狼當道，鯨鯢橫擊，海內業業，未知所從。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor Martial Emperor first founded the realm in its raw beginnings and first crossed hardship, at that time the world seethed, men had no fixed lord, wolves and jackals blocked the road, leviathans struck across the land, within the seas all trembled, not knowing whom to follow.
translations.idiomatic: When the Martial Emperor, our High Ancestor, first founded the realm amid chaos and first crossed through hardship, the world seethed. Men had no fixed lord; wolves blocked the roads and monsters ravaged the land. The whole realm trembled, not knowing whom to follow.

sentences.zh: 將軍運動微之鑒，折從衡之辯，策名委質，自托宗盟，此將軍妙算遠圖，發於衷誠者也。

translations.literal: The General exercised subtle discernment, broke the persuasions of the Vertical and Horizontal schools, registered your name and entrusted your person, and placed yourself under the clan alliance—this was the General's far-seeing calculation, springing from inner sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: You exercised subtle discernment, set aside the arts of alliance and counter-alliance, registered your allegiance, and entrusted yourself to the imperial clan. That was your far-seeing design, born of sincere loyalty.

sentences.zh: 及主上繼業，欽明睿聖，選賢與能，群臣輯睦，結將軍以維城之重，崇將軍以裂土之封，豈非宏謨廟略，推赤心於物者也。

translations.literal: When the sovereign succeeded to the enterprise, reverent, bright, and sage, choosing the worthy and employing the able, the ministers harmonious, he bound the General with the weight of guarding the realm and honored the General with enfeoffment and divided lands—is this not grand design from the ancestral temple, extending a red heart to all things?
translations.idiomatic: When our sovereign succeeded to the throne, reverent, bright, and sage, choosing the worthy and employing the able while his ministers lived in harmony, he bound you with the duty of guarding the realm and honored you with enfeoffment and broad lands. Is that not the court's grand design, extending its loyal heart to all?

sentences.zh: 屢申明詔，款篤殷勤，君臣之分定矣，骨肉之恩深矣。

translations.literal: Repeatedly clarifying edicts, sincere and earnest in kindness—the distinction of lord and minister is fixed, the affection of flesh and bone is deep.
translations.idiomatic: He has issued edict after edict, earnest and full of kindness. The bond between lord and minister is settled, and the affection between kin runs deep.

sentences.zh: 不意將軍惑于邪說，翻然異計，寄所以疾首痛心，泣盡繼之以血，萬全之策，竊為將軍惜之。

translations.literal: I did not expect the General to be deluded by perverse persuasions and suddenly change his plan; this is why Ji beats his head and grieves his heart, weeping until tears are followed by blood; the plan of perfect safety—I privately grieve for the General over it.
translations.idiomatic: I never expected you to be swayed by perverse counsel and suddenly change course. That is why I beat my head and grieve until tears are followed by blood. I grieve for you over the plan that would have kept you wholly safe.

sentences.zh: 寄雖疾侵耄及，言無足采，千慮一得，請陳愚算。

translations.literal: Though Ji's illness encroaches on old age and my words are not worth gathering, among a thousand thoughts one may hit the mark—I beg to set forth my foolish plan.
translations.idiomatic: Though my illness has brought me to old age and my words may be worthless, among a thousand thoughts one may prove true. I beg leave to set forth my humble counsel.

sentences.zh: 願將軍少戢雷霆，賒其晷刻，使得盡狂瞽之說，披肝膽之誠，則雖死之日，猶生之年也。

translations.literal: I wish the General would slightly restrain your thunder, grant a moment's delay, so that I may fully speak my reckless and blind words and lay bare the sincerity of liver and gall—then even on the day of death it would be as the years of life.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to restrain your wrath for a moment and grant me a little time, so that I may fully speak my reckless words and lay bare my loyal heart. Then even on the day I die it will be as though I still lived.

sentences.zh: 自天厭梁德，多難薦臻，寰宇分崩，英雄互起，不可勝紀，人人自以為得之。

translations.literal: Since Heaven grew weary of Liang's virtue and many hardships came in succession, the realm split apart and heroes rose against one another beyond counting; each man thought he had grasped success.
translations.idiomatic: Since Heaven grew weary of the Liang and hardships followed one upon another, the realm split apart and heroes rose beyond counting, each believing he held destiny in his hand.

sentences.zh: 然夷凶翦亂，拯溺扶危，四海樂推，三靈眷命，揖讓而居南面者，陳氏也。

translations.literal: Yet it was the Chen who quelled the barbarous and cut down disorder, rescued the drowning and upheld the endangered, were joyfully advanced by the four seas, were favored by the three numina, and through yielding ceremony took the facing-south position.
translations.idiomatic: Yet it was the house of Chen that quelled the wicked, rescued the drowning, and upheld the endangered; that the four seas joyfully advanced, that the three numina favored, and that through abdication took the throne.

sentences.zh: 豈非歷數有在，惟天所授，當璧應運，其事甚明，一也。

translations.literal: Is this not because the cycle of fate had its place and Heaven alone bestowed it—the jade disk answering the age? This matter is very clear—the first point.
translations.idiomatic: Is this not because the mandate of fate was fixed and Heaven alone bestowed it, the jade disk answering the age? This is clear—the first point.

sentences.zh: 主上承基，明德遠被，天綱再張，地維重紐。

translations.literal: The sovereign inherits the foundation; bright virtue spreads far; Heaven's net is stretched anew; Earth's cords are bound again.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign has inherited the foundation. His bright virtue spreads far. Heaven's net is stretched anew and Earth's cords are bound again.

sentences.zh: 夫以王琳之強，侯瑱之力，進足以搖盪中原，爭衡天下，退足以屈強江外，雄張偏隅。

translations.literal: Consider Wang Lin's strength and Hou Tian's power: advancing, they were enough to shake the central plains and contend for the realm; retreating, enough to bend the strong beyond the Yangzi and dominate a corner.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Wang Lin's strength and Hou Tian's power. Advancing, they could shake the central plains and contend for the realm. Retreating, they could hold the Yangzi south and dominate a corner.

sentences.zh: 然或命一旅之師，或資一士之說，琳即瓦解冰泮，投身異域，瑱則厥角稽顙，委命闕庭。

translations.literal: Yet with only a single brigade sent, or relying on one man's persuasion, Lin at once dissolved like ice melting, casting himself into foreign lands; Tian bowed forehead to ground and entrusted his fate to the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: Yet with a single brigade sent, or with one man's counsel relied upon, Lin dissolved like melting ice and fled to foreign lands, while Tian bowed his forehead to the ground and surrendered at the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 斯又天假之威，而除其患，其事甚明，二也。

translations.literal: This again is Heaven lending its might to remove their peril—this matter is very clear—the second point.
translations.idiomatic: This again is Heaven lending its might to remove such threats. This is clear—the second point.

sentences.zh: 今將軍以藩戚之重，擁東南之眾，盡忠奉上，戮力勤王，豈不勳高竇融，寵過吳芮，析珪判野，南面稱孤，其事甚明，三也。

translations.literal: Now the General, with the weight of a frontier kinsman, holds the hosts of the southeast; if you exhaust loyalty in serving above and join strength to aid the throne, would your merit not exceed Dou Rong's, your favor surpass Wu Rui's, with jade tallies divided and fields apportioned, facing south and styled solitary lord? This matter is very clear—the third point.
translations.idiomatic: You bear the weight of an imperial kinsman on the frontier and command the hosts of the southeast. If you devote your loyalty to the throne and join your strength to the royal cause, would your merit not exceed Dou Rong's and your favor surpass Wu Rui's, with jade tallies divided and lands apportioned, reigning in your domain? This is clear—the third point.

sentences.zh: 且聖朝棄瑕忘過，寬厚待人，改過自新，咸加敘擢。

translations.literal: Moreover the holy court discards flaws and forgets faults, treats men with generous breadth, and those who reform and renew themselves are all promoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the court discards flaws and forgets faults, treats men with generous breadth, and promotes all who reform and renew themselves.

sentences.zh: 至如余孝頃、潘純陀、李孝欽、歐陽頠等，悉委以心腹，任以爪牙，胸中豁然，曾無纖芥。

translations.literal: As for Yu Xiaoxiang, Pan Chuntuo, Li Xiaoqin, Ouyang Hui, and the like—all were entrusted as inner confidants and employed as claws and fangs; the breast was open and clear, never a fiber of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Yu Xiaoxiang, Pan Chuntuo, Li Xiaoqin, and Ouyang Hui were all entrusted as inner confidants and employed as his claws and fangs. The sovereign's heart remained open, without the slightest grudge.

sentences.zh: 況將軍釁非張繡，罪異畢諶，當何慮于危亡，何失于富貴？

translations.literal: How much more so for the General, whose offense is not Zhang Xiu's, whose crime differs from Bi Chen's—why should you fear ruin, why lose wealth and honor?
translations.idiomatic: Your offense is not Zhang Xiu's, your crime differs from Bi Chen's. Why should you fear ruin or lose wealth and honor?

sentences.zh: 此又其事甚明，四也。

translations.literal: This again is very clear—the fourth point.
translations.idiomatic: This too is clear—the fourth point.

sentences.zh: 方今周、齊鄰睦，境外無虞，並兵一向，匪朝伊夕。

translations.literal: At present Zhou and Qi are neighbors in harmony; beyond the borders there is no worry; united armies will strike in one direction—not merely tomorrow or the day after.
translations.idiomatic: At present Northern Zhou and Qi are friendly neighbors. Beyond the borders there is no worry, yet their united armies may strike at any moment—not merely tomorrow or the day after.

sentences.zh: 非有劉、項競逐之機，楚、趙連從之事，可得雍容高拱，坐論西伯，其事甚明，五也。

translations.literal: There is no occasion like Liu and Xiang contending, no matter like Chu and Zhao joining in alliance—you cannot at ease with hands folded sit and discourse like the Earl of the West. This is very clear—the fifth point.
translations.idiomatic: There is no occasion like Liu Bang and Xiang Yu contending for the realm, no alliance like Chu and Zhao joining forces. You cannot at ease with folded hands sit and discourse like the Earl of the West. This is clear—the fifth point.

sentences.zh: 且留將軍狼顧一隅，亟經摧衄，聲實虧喪，膽氣衰沮。

translations.literal: Moreover General Liu, wolf-glancing in one corner, has repeatedly suffered defeats; reputation and substance are diminished, courage and spirit decayed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover General Liu, holding one corner like a wolf glancing backward, has suffered defeat after defeat. His reputation is ruined and his courage broken.

sentences.zh: 高瓖、向文政、留瑜、黃子玉此數人者，將軍所知，首鼠兩端，唯利是視，其餘將帥亦可見矣。

translations.literal: Gao Rang, Xiang Wenzheng, Liu Yu, Huang Ziyu—these several men, as the General knows, are rats with two heads, looking only to profit; the rest of the commanders may likewise be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rang, Xiang Wenzheng, Liu Yu, and Huang Ziyu—these men you know well—are fence-sitters who look only to profit. The rest of your commanders are no better.

sentences.zh: 孰能被堅執銳，長驅深入，系馬埋輪，奮不顧命，以先士卒者乎？

translations.literal: Who among them can don hard armor and grasp sharp blades, drive far in deep penetration, tether horses and bury wheels, strive without regard for life, and lead before the soldiers?
translations.idiomatic: Who among them can don hard armor, grasp sharp blades, drive deep into enemy territory, tether horses and bury wheels, and charge ahead of the ranks without regard for his life?

sentences.zh: 此又其事甚明，六也。

translations.literal: This again is very clear—the sixth point.
translations.idiomatic: This too is clear—the sixth point.

sentences.zh: 且將軍之強，孰如侯景？

translations.literal: Moreover, is the General's strength equal to Hou Jing's?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, is your strength equal to Hou Jing's?

sentences.zh: 將軍之眾，孰如王琳？

translations.literal: Are the General's hosts equal to Wang Lin's?
translations.idiomatic: Are your troops equal to Wang Lin's?

sentences.zh: 武皇滅侯景於前，今上摧王琳於後，此乃天時，非復人力。

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor destroyed Hou Jing before; the present sovereign crushed Wang Lin after—this is Heaven's season, no longer human effort.
translations.idiomatic: The Martial Emperor destroyed Hou Jing before; our present sovereign crushed Wang Lin after. This is Heaven's season, not human strength alone.

sentences.zh: 且兵革已後，人皆厭亂，其孰能棄墳墓，捐妻子，出萬死不顧之計，從將軍于白刃之間乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, after arms and armor, all men are weary of disorder—who could abandon graves, cast off wife and children, adopt a plan of ten thousand deaths without regard, and follow the General between flashing blades?
translations.idiomatic: After years of war, all men are weary of disorder. Who would abandon his ancestors' graves, cast off wife and children, and follow you between flashing blades in a plan that courts ten thousand deaths?

sentences.zh: 此又其事甚明，七也。

translations.literal: This again is very clear—the seventh point.
translations.idiomatic: This too is clear—the seventh point.

sentences.zh: 曆觀前古，鑒之往事，子陽、季孟傾覆相尋，餘善、右渠危亡繼及，天命可畏，山川難恃。

translations.literal: Reviewing former ages and taking past events as mirror, Ziyang and Jimeng fell in succession, Yushan and Youqu perished one after another—Heaven's mandate is to be feared, mountains and rivers are hard to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying former ages and taking past events as mirror, Ziyang and Jimeng fell in succession, Yushan and Youqu perished one after another. Heaven's mandate is to be feared; mountains and rivers are hard to rely on.

sentences.zh: 況將軍欲以數郡之地，當天下之兵，以諸侯之資，拒天子之命，強弱逆順，可得侔乎？

translations.literal: How much more if the General wishes with the lands of a few commanderies to meet the armies of the realm, with a feudal lord's resources to refuse the Son of Heaven's command—can strength and weakness, obedience and rebellion, be matched?
translations.idiomatic: How much less can you, with the lands of a few commanderies, meet the armies of the realm, or with a feudal lord's resources refuse the Son of Heaven's command? Can strength and weakness, obedience and rebellion, be matched?

sentences.zh: 此又其事甚明，八也。

translations.literal: This again is very clear—the eighth point.
translations.idiomatic: This too is clear—the eighth point.

sentences.zh: 且非我族類，其心必異，不愛其親，豈能及物？

translations.literal: Moreover, those not of our kindred—their hearts must differ; if one does not love his kin, how can he reach to other things?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, those not of our kindred must differ in heart. If one does not love his kin, how can he care for others?

sentences.zh: 留將軍身縻國爵，子尚王姬，猶且棄天屬而弗顧，背明君而孤立，危急之日，豈能同憂共患，不背將軍者乎？

translations.literal: General Liu is bound by state rank, his son married to an imperial princess—yet he still abandons Heaven's kin without regard and turns his back on the enlightened lord to stand alone; in days of peril, how could he share worry and disaster and not turn against the General?
translations.idiomatic: General Liu holds state rank and his son is married to an imperial princess, yet he still abandons his kin and turns his back on the enlightened sovereign to stand alone. In days of peril, how could he share your worry and not turn against you?

sentences.zh: 至於師老力屈，懼誅利賞，必有韓、智晉陽之謀，張、陳井陘之事。

translations.literal: As for troops worn and strength spent, fearing punishment and coveting reward—there will surely be plots like Han and Zhi at Jinyang, affairs like Zhang and Chen at Jingxing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When troops grow weary and strength fails, when men fear punishment and covet reward, there will surely be plots like those of Han and Zhi at Jinyang and affairs like those of Zhang and Chen at Jingxing Pass.

sentences.zh: 此又其事甚明，九也。

translations.literal: This again is very clear—the ninth point.
translations.idiomatic: This too is clear—the ninth point.

sentences.zh: 且北軍萬里遠鬥，鋒不可當，將軍自戰其地，人多顧後，梁安背向為心，修忤匹夫之力，眾寡不敵，將帥不侔，師以無名而出，事以無機而動，以此稱兵，未知其利。

translations.literal: Moreover the northern army fights from ten thousand li away yet its edge cannot be withstood; the General fights on your own ground—men mostly look behind; Liang An's heart turns away; Xiu defies a common man's strength; many and few do not match, commanders are not equal; the army goes forth without righteous name, the affair moves without opportune moment—by this to raise arms, one does not know the profit.
translations.idiomatic: The northern army fights from ten thousand li away, yet its edge cannot be withstood. You fight on your own ground, yet your men look behind them. Liang An's heart has turned away. Xiu can defy only a common man's strength. Many and few do not match; commanders are unequal. Your army goes forth without righteous cause and moves without opportune moment. To raise arms on this basis—I do not see the profit.

sentences.zh: 夫以漢朝吳、楚，晉室穎、顒，連城數十，長戟百萬，拔本塞源，自圖家國，其有成功者乎？

translations.literal: Consider Han's Wu and Chu, Jin's Ying and Yong—linked cities by the tens, long halberds by the million, uprooting the root and blocking the source, plotting state and clan for themselves—were there any who succeeded?
translations.idiomatic: Consider Han's Wu and Chu, Jin's Ying and Yong—linked cities by the tens, long halberds by the million, uprooting the root and blocking the source to plot for themselves—were there any who succeeded?

sentences.zh: 此又其事甚明，十也。

translations.literal: This again is very clear—the tenth point.
translations.idiomatic: This too is clear—the tenth point.

sentences.zh: 為將軍計者，莫若不遠而復，絕親留氏，秦郎、快郎，隨遣入質，釋甲偃兵，一遵詔旨。

translations.literal: For the General's planning, nothing surpasses not going far yet returning, breaking kinship with the Liu clan, sending Qinlang and Kuailang as hostages at once, laying aside armor and resting weapons, following the edict in full.
translations.idiomatic: For your planning, nothing surpasses returning while you are still far from ruin: break with the Liu clan, send Qinlang and Kuailang as hostages at once, lay aside armor and rest your weapons, and follow the imperial edict in full.

sentences.zh: 且朝廷許以鐵券之要，申以白馬之盟，朕不食言，誓之宗社。

translations.literal: Moreover the court promises the pledge of the iron certificate and renews the white-horse covenant—We shall not eat our words, sworn before the ancestral altars.
translations.idiomatic: The court promises the pledge of the iron certificate and renews the covenant sworn over a white horse. The sovereign will not break his word; he swears it before the ancestral altars.

sentences.zh: 寄聞明者鑒未形，智者不再計，此成敗之效，將軍勿疑，吉凶之幾，間不容髮。

translations.literal: Ji has heard that the clear-sighted discern what has not yet taken form, the wise do not reckon twice—this is the effect of success and failure; the General must not doubt; the hinge of fortune and ruin admits not a hair's breadth between.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the clear-sighted discern what has not yet taken form and the wise do not reckon twice. This is the effect of success and failure. Do not doubt it. The hinge of fortune and ruin admits not a hair's breadth between.

sentences.zh: 方今蕃維尚少，皇子幼沖，凡預宗枝，皆蒙寵樹。

translations.literal: At present the frontier bulwarks are still few, the imperial sons young and tender—all who share the clan branch are showered with favor and planted in office.
translations.idiomatic: At present the frontier bulwarks are still few and the imperial sons young. All who share the imperial clan are showered with favor and planted in high office.

sentences.zh: 況以將軍之地，將軍之才，將軍之名，將軍之勢，而能克修蕃服，北面稱臣，甯與劉澤同年而語其功業哉？

translations.literal: How much more with the General's lands, the General's talent, the General's name, the General's power—if you can well cultivate your frontier service and face north as minister, could your achievements be spoken of in the same year as Liu Ze's?
translations.idiomatic: With your lands, your talent, your name, and your power, if you can well fulfill your frontier duty and face north as a loyal minister, could your achievements be spoken of in the same breath as Liu Ze's?

sentences.zh: 豈不身與山河等安，名與金石相弊？

translations.literal: Would not body share equal peace with mountains and rivers, name share equal endurance with metal and stone?
translations.idiomatic: Would not your person share the peace of mountains and rivers, your name endure like metal and stone?

sentences.zh: 願加三思，慮之無忽。

translations.literal: I wish you would add thrice-thought reflection and consider it without neglect.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to think thrice and not neglect this counsel.

sentences.zh: 寄氣力綿微，余陰無幾，感恩懷德，不覺狂言，鈇鉞之誅，甘之如薺。

translations.literal: Ji's breath and strength are thread-thin, remaining shade not many; grateful for kindness and cherishing virtue, without noticing I speak wildly—the axe and halberd punishment I would accept as sweet as shepherd's purse.
translations.idiomatic: My strength is thread-thin and my days few. Grateful for your kindness, I have spoken rashly without noticing. I would accept the axe and halberd as gladly as shepherd's purse.

sentences.zh: 寶應覽書大怒。

translations.literal: Baoying read the letter and was greatly angry.
translations.idiomatic: Baoying read the letter and flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 或謂寶應曰：「虞公病篤，言多錯謬。」

translations.literal: Someone said to Baoying: "Lord Yu's illness is grave; his words are mostly mistaken."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Baoying, "Lord Yu is gravely ill. His words are mostly delirious."

sentences.zh: 寶應意乃小釋。

translations.literal: Baoying's mind then eased a little.
translations.idiomatic: Baoying's anger eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 亦以寄人望，且容之。

translations.literal: Also because of Ji's public esteem, he tolerated him for the time.
translations.idiomatic: He also spared Ji for a time out of respect for his reputation.

sentences.zh: 及寶應敗走，夜至蒲田，顧謂其子扞秦曰：「早從虞公計，不至今日。」

translations.literal: When Baoying was defeated and fled, by night he reached Putian, turned and said to his son Hanchin: "Had we early followed Lord Yu's plan, we would not have come to today."
translations.idiomatic: When Baoying was defeated and fled, he reached Putian by night and turned to his son Hanchin. "Had we followed Lord Yu's counsel earlier, we would not have come to this."

sentences.zh: 扞秦但泣而已。

translations.literal: Hanchin only wept, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Hanchin could only weep.

sentences.zh: 寶應既禽，凡諸賓客微有交涉者皆誅，唯寄以先識免禍。

translations.literal: When Baoying was captured, all guests who had even slight dealings were executed; only Ji, through prior understanding, escaped calamity.
translations.idiomatic: After Baoying was captured, every guest who had had even slight dealings with him was executed. Only Ji escaped, thanks to his earlier remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 初，沙門慧標涉獵有才思，及寶應起兵，作五言詩以送之曰：「送馬猶臨水，離旗稍引風。

translations.literal: Earlier, the monk Huibiao, broadly versed and with literary wit, when Baoying raised troops composed a five-word poem to send him off, saying: "Seeing off the horses still by the water, the parting banners slightly catch the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the monk Huibiao, widely read and clever, composed a five-word poem when Baoying raised troops to send him off: "Horses still water at the ford; parting banners catch the wind.

sentences.zh: 好看今夜月，當照紫微宮。」

translations.literal: Watch well tonight's moon—it should shine on the Purple Subtlety Palace."
translations.idiomatic: Watch well tonight's moon—it shall shine on the Purple Subtlety Palace."

sentences.zh: 寶應得之甚悅。

translations.literal: Baoying received it and was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Baoying was greatly pleased by it.

sentences.zh: 慧標以示寄，寄一覽便止，正色無言。

translations.literal: Huibiao showed it to Ji; Ji glanced once and stopped, stern in countenance without speech.
translations.idiomatic: Huibiao showed it to Ji. Ji read it once, set it down, and said nothing, his face stern.

sentences.zh: 慧標退，寄謂所親曰：「標公既以此始，必以此終。」

translations.literal: When Huibiao withdrew, Ji told those close to him: "Master Biao has begun with this—he will surely end with it."
translations.idiomatic: When Huibiao withdrew, Ji told those close to him, "Master Biao has begun with this—he will surely end with it."

sentences.zh: 後竟坐是誅。

translations.literal: In the end he was indeed executed on this account.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was indeed executed for it.

sentences.zh: 文帝尋敕都督章昭達發遣寄還朝，及至，謂曰：「管寧無恙，甚慰勞懷。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen soon ordered Area Commander Zhang Zhaoda to send Ji back to court; when he arrived, the Emperor said: "Guan Ning is unharmed—greatly comforting to my weary heart."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen soon ordered Area Commander Zhang Zhaoda to send Ji back to court. When he arrived, the Emperor said, "Like Guan Ning you have returned safe and sound—this greatly comforts my weary heart."

sentences.zh: 頃之，帝謂到仲舉曰：「衡陽王既出合，須得一人旦夕遊處，兼掌書記，宜求宿士有行業者。」

translations.literal: Before long the Emperor said to Dao Zhongju: "Now that the Prince of Hengyang has left the Terrace, we need a man to accompany him morning and evening and also take charge of secretarial work—one should seek an elder scholar of established conduct."
translations.idiomatic: Soon after the Emperor told Dao Zhongju, "Now that the Prince of Hengyang has left the capital, we need someone to keep him company day and night and handle his secretarial work. We should find an elder scholar of established conduct."

sentences.zh: 仲舉未知所對，帝曰：「吾自得之。」

translations.literal: Zhongju did not know how to answer; the Emperor said: "I have already found him myself."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongju did not know whom to name. The Emperor said, "I have already chosen him."

sentences.zh: 乃手敕用寄。

translations.literal: He then by handwritten edict employed Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He then by handwritten edict appointed Ji.

sentences.zh: 寄入謝，帝曰：「所以暫屈卿遊蕃，非止以文翰相煩，乃令以師表相事也。」

translations.literal: Ji entered to give thanks; the Emperor said: "The reason for temporarily bending you to travel in the frontier is not merely to trouble you with documents—it is to have you serve as teacher and model."
translations.idiomatic: Ji came to give thanks. The Emperor said, "The reason I bend you for a time to the frontier is not merely to burden you with documents. I wish you to serve as teacher and model."

sentences.zh: 後除東中郎建安王諮議，加戎昭將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was made Staff Adviser to the Eastern Central Commandant, Prince of Jian'an, with additional rank as General of Martial Illumination.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Staff Adviser to the Prince of Jian'an, Eastern Central Commandant, with the additional rank of General of Martial Illumination.

sentences.zh: 寄乃辭以疾，不堪旦夕陪列。

translations.literal: Ji then declined on grounds of illness, unable to bear attendance morning and evening in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Ji declined on grounds of illness, saying he could not bear constant attendance in the prince's retinue.

sentences.zh: 王於是令長停公事，其有疑議，就以決之，但朔旦箋修而已。

translations.literal: The prince thereupon ordered the chief clerk to suspend routine business; when there were doubtful matters, Ji decided them—only on the first of the month did he draft memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The prince then ordered routine business suspended in the bureau. When doubts arose, Ji decided them. He drafted memorials only on the first of each month.

sentences.zh: 太建八年，加太中大夫，後卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taijian he was made Grand Master of the Palace, and later died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taijian he was made Grand Master of the Palace. He died not long after.

sentences.zh: 寄少篤行，造次必于仁厚，雖僮豎未嘗加以聲色。

translations.literal: Ji from youth was steadfast in conduct; even in haste he was always benevolent and generous; even to servants and boys he never used harsh voice or look.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Ji was steadfast in conduct. Even in haste he was always benevolent and generous, and he never raised his voice or scowled at servants or boys.

sentences.zh: 至臨危執節，則辭氣凜然，白刃不憚也。

translations.literal: When facing peril and holding to integrity, his words and bearing were stern and awe-inspiring; he did not fear naked blades.
translations.idiomatic: When facing peril he held to his integrity with stern bearing and feared no naked blade.

sentences.zh: 自流寓南土，與兄荔隔絕，因感氣病。

translations.literal: From the time he drifted and lodged in the southern lands, cut off from his elder brother Li, he thereby contracted a qi illness.
translations.idiomatic: After he was stranded in the south, cut off from his elder brother Li, he contracted a disorder of the vital breath.

sentences.zh: 每得荔書，氣輒奔劇，危殆者數矣。

translations.literal: Whenever he received a letter from Li, his qi would surge violently; several times he was in peril of death.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a letter arrived from Li, his disorder would flare violently, and several times he was near death.

sentences.zh: 前後所居官，未嘗至秩滿，裁期月，便自求解退。

translations.literal: In all offices he held before and after, he never reached a full term—only a month or so and he would himself request to resign and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: In every office he held he never served a full term. After only a month or so he would request resignation.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「知足不辱，吾知足矣。」

translations.literal: He often said: "Knowing sufficiency brings no disgrace—I know sufficiency."
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "Knowing when one has enough brings no disgrace. I know when I have enough."

sentences.zh: 及謝病私庭，每諸王為州將，下車必造門致禮，命釋鞭板，以几杖侍坐。

translations.literal: When he resigned for illness to his private courtyard, whenever a prince became a provincial commander, on dismounting he would certainly visit the gate to pay respects, ordering whip and tablet set aside and attending seated with armrest and staff.
translations.idiomatic: When he retired ill to his home, every prince who became a provincial commander would visit his gate on arrival, set aside whip and tablet, and sit with him using armrest and staff as for an elder.

sentences.zh: 嘗出遊近寺，閭里傳相告語，老幼羅列，望拜道左。

translations.literal: Once going out to visit a nearby temple, the lanes and hamlets passed word to one another; old and young lined up and bowed from the left of the road in greeting.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he went out to a nearby temple, word spread through the neighborhood. Old and young lined the road and bowed as he passed.

sentences.zh: 或言誓為約者，但指寄便不欺，其至行所感如此。

translations.literal: Some said that in sworn agreements, merely pointing to Ji meant no deceit—such was the feeling stirred by his utmost conduct.
translations.idiomatic: People said that in sworn agreements, merely naming Ji as witness meant no deceit would follow—such was the power of his moral example.

sentences.zh: 所制文筆，遭亂並多散失。

translations.literal: The writings he composed, amid the turmoil, were mostly scattered and lost.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the writings he composed were scattered and lost in the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 傅縡字宜事，北地靈州人也。

translations.literal: Fu Zai, courtesy name Yishi, was a native of Lingzhou in Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zai, whose courtesy name was Yishi, came from Lingzhou in Beidi commandery.

sentences.zh: 父彝，梁臨沂令。

translations.literal: His father Yi was Magistrate of Linyi under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi had served the Liang as Magistrate of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 縡幼聰敏，七歲誦古詩賦至十餘萬言。

translations.literal: Zai in youth was clever and keen; at seven he could recite ancient poetry and rhapsodies to more than a hundred thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Zai was quick-witted. At seven he could recite more than a hundred thousand words of ancient poetry and rhapsodies.

sentences.zh: 長好學，能屬文。

translations.literal: When grown he loved learning and could compose.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he loved learning and wrote with skill.

sentences.zh: 太清末，丁母憂，在兵亂中，居喪盡禮，哀毀骨立，士友以此稱之。

translations.literal: At the end of Taiqing he entered mourning for his mother; amid military disorder he observed mourning with full rites, grief wasting him to bone-standing; scholar friends praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Taiqing era he mourned his mother. Amid military disorder he observed the full rites of mourning until grief had wasted him to skin and bone, and his friends praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 後依湘州刺史蕭循。

translations.literal: Later he relied on Xiangzhou Inspector Xiao Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Later he attached himself to Xiao Xun, Inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 循頗好士，廣集墳籍，縡肆志尋閱，因博通群書。

translations.literal: Xun greatly favored scholars and broadly gathered classical texts; Zai followed his will in searching and reading, and thereby mastered all books.
translations.idiomatic: Xun greatly favored scholars and gathered a broad library. Zai read at will and thereby mastered the classics.

sentences.zh: 王琳聞其名，引為府記室。

translations.literal: Wang Lin heard his name and brought him in as Registrar of the princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin heard of him and appointed him Registrar on his staff.

sentences.zh: 琳敗，隨琳將孫瑒還都。

translations.literal: When Lin was defeated, he followed Lin's general Sun Chang back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin was defeated, he followed Lin's general Sun Chang back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時陳文帝使顏晃賜瑒雜物，瑒托縡啟謝，詞理周洽，文無加點。

translations.literal: At the time Chen Emperor Wen sent Yan Huang to bestow sundry goods on Chang; Chang entrusted Zai to draft the letter of thanks—its reasoning complete and rounded, the text needing no dot of correction.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Wen sent Yan Huang to bestow gifts on Sun Chang. Chang asked Zai to draft the letter of thanks. Its reasoning was complete and the prose flawless.

sentences.zh: 晃還言之文帝，召為撰史學士。

translations.literal: When Huang returned he told Emperor Wen, who summoned Zai as Historiography Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Huang reported this to Emperor Wen on his return, and Zai was summoned as Historiography Scholar.

sentences.zh: 再遷驃騎安成王中記室，撰史如故。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Central Recorder under the Rapid Cavalry General, Prince of Ancheng, with historiography as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Central Recorder to the Prince of Ancheng, Rapid Cavalry General, while continuing his historiographical duties.

sentences.zh: 縡篤信佛教，從興皇寺慧朗法師受三論，盡通其學。

translations.literal: Zai devoutly believed in Buddhism; from Master Huilang of Xinghuang Temple he received the Three Treatises and fully mastered the teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Zai was a devout Buddhist. He studied the Three Treatises under Master Huilang of Xinghuang Temple and mastered the doctrine completely.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官兼通直散騎侍郎使齊，還，累遷太子庶子、僕。

translations.literal: Soon with his original office he was additionally made Regular Attendant of the Direct and Upright Cavalry and sent as envoy to Qi; on return he was repeatedly promoted to Crown Prince Attendant and Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally appointed Regular Attendant of the Direct and Upright Cavalry and sent as envoy to Qi. On his return he rose through Crown Prince Attendant to Vice Director of the Crown Prince's household.

sentences.zh: 後主即位，遷秘書監、右衛將軍，兼中書通事舍人，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: When the Later Sovereign succeeded, Zai was moved to Director of the Secretariat, General of the Right Guard, and concurrent Secretariat Communications Attendant, in charge of edicts and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Sovereign succeeded, Zai became Director of the Secretariat and General of the Right Guard, with concurrent duty as Secretariat Communications Attendant in charge of edicts and proclamations.

sentences.zh: 縡為文典麗，性又敏速，雖軍國大事，下筆輒成，未嘗起草，沈思者亦無以加，甚為後主所重。

translations.literal: Zai's writing was classical and elegant, his nature also quick and nimble; even in great military and state affairs, the brush at once produced completion, never drafting first—even deep thinkers could not surpass him; the Later Sovereign greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Zai wrote in a classical, elegant style and worked with remarkable speed. Even on grave military and state matters his pen produced finished prose at once, without drafting. Even the most deliberate writers could not match him, and the Later Sovereign valued him deeply.

sentences.zh: 然性木強，不持檢操，負才使氣，陵侮人物，朝士多銜之。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was woodenly stubborn; he did not restrain himself; he relied on talent and vented temper, insulting others; court gentlemen mostly harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was stubborn by nature, unrestrained in conduct, arrogant in his gifts, and insulting toward others. Most court officials bore him a grudge.

sentences.zh: 會施文慶、沈客卿以佞見幸，專制衡軸，而縡益疏。

translations.literal: It happened that Shi Wenqing and Shen Keqing, through flattery gaining favor, monopolized the hubs of power, while Zai grew ever more distant.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wenqing and Shen Keqing won favor through flattery and monopolized the centers of power, while Zai grew ever more distant from court.

sentences.zh: 文慶等因共譖之，後主收縡下獄。

translations.literal: Wenqing and the rest therefore slandered him together; the Later Sovereign seized Zai and put him in prison.
translations.idiomatic: They slandered him together, and the Later Sovereign had Zai arrested and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 縡素剛，因憤恚，於獄中上書曰：「夫人君者，恭事上帝，子愛黔黎，省嗜欲，遠諂佞，未明求衣，日旰忘食，是以澤被區宇，慶流子孫。

translations.literal: Zai had always been upright; in indignant rage, from prison he submitted a memorial saying: "Now the lord of men should reverently serve the Supreme Lord, treat the black-haired people as children, reduce appetites and desires, keep far from flatterers, seek robes before dawn is clear, forget food as the sun tilts—thus grace covers the realm and blessing flows to descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Zai had always been upright. In rage he submitted a memorial from prison: "A ruler should reverently serve Heaven, love the people as his children, curb his appetites, keep flatterers at a distance, rise before dawn, and forget his meal as the sun tilts west. Thus grace covers the realm and blessing flows to his descendants.

sentences.zh: 陛下頃來酒色過度，不虔郊廟之神，專媚淫昏之鬼。

translations.literal: Your Majesty of late has wine and women in excess, is not reverent to the gods of suburban altars and ancestral temples, and devotes yourself only to lewd and benighted spirits.
