translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty of late has indulged excessively in wine and women, neglected the gods of the suburban altars and ancestral temples, and devoted yourself to lewd and benighted spirits.

sentences.zh: 小人在側，宦豎弄權，惡忠直若仇讎，視百姓如草芥。

translations.literal: Petty men are at your side, eunuch attendants toy with power, you hate the loyal and upright as enemies, and regard the hundred surnames as grass and husks.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men stand at your side, eunuchs toy with power, you hate the loyal and upright as enemies, and regard the common people as grass and chaff.

sentences.zh: 後宮曳綺繡，廄馬餘菽粟，兆庶流離，轉屍蔽野，貨賄公行，帑藏損耗，神怒人怨，眾叛親離。

translations.literal: The rear palace trails brocade and embroidery, stable horses have surplus beans and grain, the myriad people wander displaced, corpses turned over cover the wilds, bribes walk openly, the treasury is drained, gods are angry and men resent, the masses rebel and kin depart.
translations.idiomatic: The rear palace trails brocade while the stables overflow with grain. The people wander displaced; corpses cover the fields. Bribes walk openly and the treasury is drained. Gods are angry, men resent you, the masses rebel, and your kin turn away.

sentences.zh: 恐東南王氣，自斯而盡。」

translations.literal: I fear the kingly qi of the southeast will from this be exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: I fear the kingly qi of the southeast will from this moment be exhausted."

sentences.zh: 書奏，後主大怒。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted, and the Later Ruler was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, and the Later Ruler was greatly angered.

sentences.zh: 書奏，後主大怒。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Later Sovereign was greatly angry.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the Later Sovereign flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 頃之稍解，使謂曰：「我欲赦卿，卿能改過不？」

translations.literal: Before long his anger eased somewhat; he sent word: "I wish to pardon you—can you reform your faults?"
translations.idiomatic: Before long his anger eased. He sent word: "I wish to pardon you. Can you reform your ways?"

sentences.zh: 縡對曰：「臣心如面，臣面可改，則臣心可改。」

translations.literal: Zai replied: "Your servant's heart is like his face—if my face could be changed, then my heart could be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Zai replied, "My heart is like my face. If my face could be changed, then my heart could be changed."

sentences.zh: 後主於是益怒，令宦者李善度窮其事，賜死獄中。

translations.literal: The Later Sovereign thereupon grew angrier still, ordered the eunuch Li Shandu to investigate the matter fully, and granted death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Sovereign grew still angrier, ordered the eunuch Li Shandu to investigate the matter fully, and had him executed in prison.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: A collection of his writings in ten juan circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 縡雖強直有才，而毒惡傲慢，為當世所疾。

translations.literal: Though Zai was forcefully upright and talented, he was venomous, wicked, and arrogant, and was resented by his age.
translations.idiomatic: Though forcefully upright and talented, Zai was venomous and arrogant, and his contemporaries resented him.

sentences.zh: 及死，有惡蛇屈尾來上靈床，當前受祭酹，去而復來者百餘日。

translations.literal: When he died, a vicious serpent with curled tail came onto the spirit couch, received offerings and libations before it, left and returned for more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: After his death a vicious serpent with curled tail came onto his spirit couch, accepted offerings before it, and returned day after day for more than a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 時時有彈指聲。

translations.literal: From time to time there was the sound of finger-snapping.
translations.idiomatic: From time to time there was also the sound of finger-snapping.

sentences.zh: 時有吳興章華，字仲宗，家本農夫，至華獨好學，與士君子游處，頗通經史，善屬文。

translations.literal: At the time there was Zhang Hua of Wuxing, courtesy name Zhongzong; his family were originally farmers, but Hua alone loved learning, associated with gentlemen and scholars, was fairly versed in the classics and histories, and skilled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was Zhang Hua of Wuxing, courtesy name Zhongzong. His family were farmers, but he alone loved learning, kept company with scholars, was well versed in the classics and histories, and wrote with skill.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，游嶺南，居羅浮山寺，專精習業。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's turmoil he traveled to Lingnan and dwelt at Luofu Mountain Temple, devoting himself wholly to study.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion he went to Lingnan and lived at Luofu Mountain Temple, devoting himself wholly to study.

sentences.zh: 歐陽頠為廣州刺史，署為南海太守。

translations.literal: When Ouyang Hui was Inspector of Guangzhou, he appointed Hua Administrator of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: When Ouyang Hui became Inspector of Guangzhou, he appointed Hua Administrator of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 頠子紇敗，乃還都。

translations.literal: When Hui's son He was defeated, Hua then returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui's son He was defeated, Hua returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 後主時，除太市令，非其所好，乃辭以疾。

translations.literal: Under the Later Sovereign he was made Director of the Grand Market—not to his liking, so he declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Sovereign he was appointed Director of the Grand Market, a post he disliked, and he declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 禎明初，上書極諫，其大略曰：「陛下即位，於今五年，不思先帝之艱難，不知天命之可畏。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenming he submitted a memorial of utmost remonstrance; its general purport said: "Your Majesty has reigned now five years, not reflecting on the former emperor's hardships, not knowing that Heaven's mandate is to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenming era he submitted a memorial of the strongest remonstrance, which in essence read: "Your Majesty has reigned five years without reflecting on the former emperor's hardships or knowing that Heaven's mandate is to be feared.

sentences.zh: 溺于嬖寵，惑於酒色。

translations.literal: Drowned in favorites, deluded by wine and women.
translations.idiomatic: You are drowned in favorites and deluded by wine and women.

sentences.zh: 祠七廟而不出，拜妃嬪而臨軒。

translations.literal: You sacrifice at the seven temples yet do not go forth; you bow to consorts and concubines yet ascend the hall.
translations.idiomatic: You neglect the sacrifices at the seven temples yet attend to your consorts at court.

sentences.zh: 老臣宿將，棄之草莽，諂佞讒邪，升之朝廷。

translations.literal: Old ministers and veteran generals you cast into the wild grass; flatterers, sycophants, slanderers, and the wicked you raise to the court.
translations.idiomatic: You cast old ministers and veteran generals into the wilderness while raising flatterers and slanderers to the court.

sentences.zh: 今疆埸日蹙，隋軍壓境，陛下如不改弦易張，臣見麋鹿復游于姑蘇矣。」

translations.literal: Now the borders daily shrink and Sui armies press the frontier; if Your Majesty does not change the strings and stretch anew, your servant sees elk and deer roaming Gusu again."
translations.idiomatic: The borders shrink daily and Sui armies press the frontier. If Your Majesty does not change course, I see elk roaming Gusu once more."

sentences.zh: 書奏，後主大怒，即日斬之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Later Sovereign was greatly angry and executed him that same day.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the Later Sovereign flew into a rage and executed him that same day.

sentences.zh: 顧野王字希馮，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Gu Yewang, courtesy name Xifeng, was a native of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yewang, whose courtesy name was Xifeng, came from Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖子喬，梁東中郎武陵王府參軍事。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ziqiao was a staff officer in the Liang Eastern Central Commandant's establishment of the Prince of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ziqiao had served as a staff officer in the establishment of the Liang Prince of Wuling, Eastern Central Commandant.

sentences.zh: 父烜，信威臨賀王記室，兼本郡五官掾，以儒術知名。

translations.literal: His father Xuan was Recorder for the Prince of Linhe, Trustworthy in Might, and concurrent Commandery Five-Officials Assistant, renowned for Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuan had been Recorder to the Prince of Linhe, Trustworthy in Might, with concurrent duty as Commandery Five-Officials Assistant, and was renowned for Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 野王幼好學，七歲讀五經，略知大旨。

translations.literal: Yewang from youth loved learning; at seven he read the Five Classics and grasped their main purport.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Yewang loved learning. At seven he read the Five Classics and grasped their main purport.

sentences.zh: 九歲能屬文。

translations.literal: At nine he could compose.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he could already compose.

sentences.zh: 嘗制日賦，領軍朱異見而奇之。

translations.literal: Once he composed a Rhapsody on the Sun; Area Commander Zhu Yi saw it and marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Once he composed a Rhapsody on the Sun. Area Commander Zhu Yi saw it and was astonished.

sentences.zh: 十二，隨父之建安，撰建安地記二篇。

translations.literal: At twelve, following his father to Jian'an, he composed two chapters of a Topography of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he accompanied his father to Jian'an and composed two chapters of a Topography of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 長而遍觀經史，精記默識，天文地理，蓍龜占候，蟲篆奇字，無所不通。

translations.literal: When grown he surveyed the classics and histories broadly, memorized with fine retention and silent recall; astronomy and geography, yarrow and tortoise divination, insect-seal and strange characters—there was nothing he did not master.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he read widely in the classics and histories with remarkable memory. Astronomy, geography, yarrow and tortoise divination, seal script and rare characters—there was nothing he did not master.

sentences.zh: 為臨賀王府記室。

translations.literal: He became Recorder in the Prince of Linhe's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He became Recorder in the establishment of the Prince of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 宣城王為揚州刺史，野王及琅邪王褒並為賓客，王甚愛其才。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Xuancheng was Inspector of Yangzhou, Yewang and Wang Bao of Langya were both his guests; the prince greatly loved their talent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Xuancheng became Inspector of Yangzhou, Yewang and Wang Bao of Langya both served as his guests, and the prince greatly prized their talents.

sentences.zh: 野王又善丹青，王於東府起齋，令野王畫古賢，命王褒書贊，時人稱為二絕。

translations.literal: Yewang was also skilled in cinnabar and green; the prince built a studio in the eastern mansion, had Yewang paint ancient worthies and ordered Wang Bao to inscribe encomia—men of the time called them twin marvels.
translations.idiomatic: Yewang was also skilled in painting. The prince built a studio in the eastern mansion, had Yewang paint ancient worthies, and ordered Wang Bao to inscribe their encomia. Contemporaries called them twin marvels.

sentences.zh: 及侯景之亂，野王丁父憂，歸本郡，乃召募鄉黨，隨義軍援都。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing's turmoil came, Yewang entered mourning for his father, returned to his home commandery, then recruited township and district men and followed the loyal army to aid the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion Yewang mourned his father, returned home, recruited local men, and marched with the loyal army to relieve the capital.

sentences.zh: 野王體素清羸，裁長六尺，又居喪過毀，殆不勝哀。

translations.literal: Yewang's frame was by nature slight and lean, barely six feet tall; moreover in mourning he exceeded proper grief and could scarcely bear his sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Yewang was slight and frail by nature, barely six feet tall, and his mourning had wasted him until he could scarcely bear his grief.

sentences.zh: 及杖戈被甲，陳君臣之義，逆順之理，抗辭作色，見者莫不壯之。

translations.literal: Yet when he took staff and spear and donned armor, setting forth the principle of lord and minister, the logic of obedience and rebellion, with defiant words and stern countenance—all who saw were stirred to admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when he took up arms and donned armor, expounding the bond between lord and minister and the logic of loyalty and rebellion with defiant words and stern bearing, all who saw him were stirred.

sentences.zh: 城陷，逃歸會稽。

translations.literal: When the city fell, he fled back to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he fled back to Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 陳天嘉中，敕補撰史學士。

translations.literal: In Chen's Tianjia era, by edict he was appointed Historiography Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianjia era he was appointed Historiography Scholar by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 太建中，為太子率更令，尋領大著作，掌國史，知梁史事。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era he was Crown Prince Director of Palace Standards, soon headed the Grand Historiographer's office, managed the national history, and oversaw Liang historical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taijian era he became Crown Prince Director of Palace Standards, soon took charge of the Grand Historiographer's office, managed the national history, and oversaw Liang historical affairs.

sentences.zh: 後為黃門侍郎，光祿卿，知五禮事。

translations.literal: Later he was Yellow Gate Vice Director, Minister of Imperial Largess, and oversaw the Five Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Yellow Gate Vice Director and Minister of Imperial Largess with oversight of the Five Rites.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈秘書監，右衛將軍。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Director of the Secretariat and General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He died. Posthumously he was made Director of the Secretariat and General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 野王少以篤學至性知名，在物無過辭失色。

translations.literal: Yewang from youth was known for devoted learning and utmost nature; among others he never overstepped in words or lost composure.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yewang was known for devoted learning and moral seriousness. In company he never spoke out of turn or lost composure.

sentences.zh: 觀其容貌，似不能言，其厲精力行，皆人所莫及。

translations.literal: To observe his appearance, he seemed unable to speak; yet his stern energy and forceful conduct were what others could not match.
translations.idiomatic: To look at him one might think he could scarcely speak, yet his stern energy and forceful conduct were beyond others' reach.

sentences.zh: 所撰玉篇三十卷，輿地志三十卷，符瑞圖十卷，顧氏譜傳十卷，分野樞要一卷，續洞冥記一卷，玄象表一卷，並行于時。

translations.literal: Works he composed: Jade Chapters in thirty juan, Topography in thirty juan, Charts of Omens and Blessings in ten juan, Gu Clan Genealogy in ten juan, Essentials of Field Allocation in one juan, Continuation of Records of the Hidden Realm in one juan, Tables of Dark Images in one juan—all circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His works included Jade Chapters in thirty juan, Topography in thirty juan, Charts of Omens and Blessings in ten juan, Gu Clan Genealogy in ten juan, Essentials of Field Allocation, Continuation of Records of the Hidden Realm, and Tables of Dark Images—all circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 又撰通史要略一百卷，國史紀傳二百卷，未就而卒。

translations.literal: He also composed Essentials of the Comprehensive History in one hundred juan and National History in Annals-Biography Form in two hundred juan, unfinished at death.
translations.idiomatic: He also began Essentials of the Comprehensive History in one hundred juan and National History in Annals-Biography Form in two hundred juan, but died before completing them.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a literary collection in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: A literary collection of twenty juan circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 時有蕭濟字孝康，東海蘭陵人也。

translations.literal: At the time there was Xiao Ji, courtesy name Xiaokang, a native of Lanling in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was Xiao Ji, courtesy name Xiaokang, from Lanling in Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 好學，博通經史。

translations.literal: He loved learning and was broadly versed in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and was broadly versed in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 仕梁為太子舍人。

translations.literal: Under Liang he served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 預平侯景功，封松陽縣侯。

translations.literal: He shared in pacifying Hou Jing and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Songyang county.
translations.idiomatic: He shared in pacifying Hou Jing and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Songyang county.

sentences.zh: 陳文帝為會稽太守，以濟為宣毅府長史。

translations.literal: When Chen Emperor Wen was Administrator of Kuaiji, he made Ji Chief Secretary of the Firm Resolution Establishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was Administrator of Kuaiji, he made Ji chief secretary of the firm-resolution establishment.

sentences.zh: 及即位，授侍中。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, Ji was appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, Ji was appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 太建中，歷位五兵、度支、祠部三尚書，卒。

translations.literal: During the Taijian era he successively held the three posts of Minister of Armaments, Minister of Revenue, and Minister of Rites, then died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taijian era he successively served as Minister of Armaments, Minister of Revenue, and Minister of Rites, then died.

sentences.zh: 姚察字伯審，吳興武康人，吳太常卿信之九世孫也。

translations.literal: Yao Cha, courtesy name Boshen, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing, ninth-generation descendant of Wu Grand Master of Ceremonies Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Cha, whose courtesy name was Boshen, came from Wukang in Wuxing. He was ninth in descent from Xin, Grand Master of Ceremonies of Wu.

sentences.zh: 父僧垣，梁太醫正。

translations.literal: His father Sengyuan was Liang Chief Physician.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sengyuan had served the Liang as Chief Physician.

sentences.zh: 及元帝在荊州，為晉安王諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan was in Jingzhou, he was Staff Adviser to the Prince of Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan was in Jingzhou, Sengyuan served as Staff Adviser to the Prince of Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 後入周，位遇甚重。

translations.literal: Later he entered Zhou and was treated with very great honor.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went over to the Northern Zhou and was treated with great honor.

sentences.zh: 察幼有至性，六歲誦書萬餘言。

translations.literal: Cha from youth had utmost nature; at six he could recite books to more than ten thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Cha showed exceptional moral seriousness. At six he could recite more than ten thousand words of text.

sentences.zh: 不好戲弄，勵精學業，十二能屬文。

translations.literal: He did not care for play and jest, urged himself in studies, and at twelve could compose.
translations.idiomatic: He disliked play, applied himself diligently to study, and at twelve could compose.

sentences.zh: 僧垣精醫術，知名梁代，二宮所得供賜，皆回給察兄弟，為遊學之資。

translations.literal: Sengyuan was skilled in medicine, renowned in the Liang age; gifts received from the two palaces he all turned over to Cha and his brothers as funds for traveling study.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan was skilled in medicine and renowned under the Liang. The gifts he received from the two palaces he gave entirely to Cha and his brothers to fund their studies abroad.

sentences.zh: 察並用聚蓄圖書，由是聞見日博。

translations.literal: Cha used it all to gather and store books; thereby his knowledge and experience daily broadened.
translations.idiomatic: Cha used these funds to gather books, and his knowledge grew broader day by day.

sentences.zh: 年十三，梁簡文帝時在東宮，盛修文義，即引于宣猷堂聽講論難，為儒者所稱。

translations.literal: At thirteen, when Liang Emperor Jianwen was in the Eastern Palace and greatly cultivated literary doctrine, Cha was brought into the Hall of Proclaimed Teachings to hear lectures and debate, and was praised by Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen, when Emperor Jianwen of Liang was cultivating literary studies in the Eastern Palace, Cha was brought into the Hall of Proclaimed Teachings to hear lectures and join debate, and Confucian scholars praised him.

sentences.zh: 及簡文嗣位，尤加禮接。

translations.literal: When Jianwen succeeded, he was especially honored in reception.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianwen succeeded to the throne, he honored Cha still more.

sentences.zh: 起家南海王國左常侍，兼司文侍郎。

translations.literal: He began his career as Left Regular Attendant in the Prince of Nanhai's establishment, and concurrent Vice Director of the Documents Office.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Left Regular Attendant in the establishment of the Prince of Nanhai with concurrent duty as Vice Director of the Documents Office.

sentences.zh: 後兼尚書駕部郎。

translations.literal: Later he was concurrently Lang of the Secretariat Carriage Section.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served concurrently as Lang of the Secretariat Carriage Section.

sentences.zh: 遇梁室喪亂，隨二親還鄉里。

translations.literal: When the Liang house fell into ruin and disorder, he followed both parents back to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang fell into chaos, he returned home with both parents.

sentences.zh: 在亂離間，篤學不廢。

translations.literal: Amid separation in turmoil, he studied devotedly without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Amid the turmoil he studied devotedly without ceasing.

sentences.zh: 元帝於荊州即位，授察原鄉令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan took the throne at Jingzhou, he appointed Cha Magistrate of Yuanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan took the throne at Jingzhou, he appointed Cha Magistrate of Yuanxiang.

sentences.zh: 後為佐著作，撰史。

translations.literal: Later he was Assistant Author and compiled history.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Assistant Author and compiled history.

sentences.zh: 陳永定中，吏部尚書徐陵領大著作，復引為史佐。

translations.literal: In Chen's Yongding era, Minister of Personnel Xu Ling headed the Grand Historiographer's office and again brought him in as history assistant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongding era Xu Ling, Minister of Personnel, headed the Grand Historiographer's office and again brought Cha in as history assistant.

sentences.zh: 太建初，補宣明殿學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taijian he was appointed Scholar of the Hall of Illuminated Proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taijian he was appointed Scholar of the Hall of Illuminated Proclamation.

sentences.zh: 尋為通直散騎常侍，報聘于周。

translations.literal: Soon he was Regular Attendant of the Direct and Upright Cavalry and returned courtesy on a mission to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Regular Attendant of the Direct and Upright Cavalry and went on a return mission to the Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 江左耆舊先在關右者，咸相傾慕。

translations.literal: Elders of the left of the Yangzi who were already in the Guan west all inclined toward him in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Elder scholars of the south who were already in the northwest all admired him.

sentences.zh: 沛國劉臻竊於公館訪漢書疑事十餘條，並為剖析，皆有經據。

translations.literal: Liu Zhen of Pei, privately at the guest house, inquired about more than ten doubtful points in the Book of Han; Cha analyzed them all, each with canonical grounding.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen of Pei privately raised more than ten doubtful points from the Book of Han at the guest house. Cha analyzed each with canonical grounding.

sentences.zh: 臻謂所親曰：「名下定無虛士。」

translations.literal: Zhen told those close to him: "When the name is settled, there is certainly no empty gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen told those close to him, "When a name is established, the man behind it is never hollow."

sentences.zh: 著西聘道里記。

translations.literal: He composed a Record of Routes on the Western Mission.
translations.idiomatic: He composed a Record of Routes on the Western Mission.

sentences.zh: 使還，補東宮學士，遷尚書祠部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, he was appointed Eastern Palace Scholar and promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat Rites Section.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Eastern Palace Scholar and promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat Rites Section.

sentences.zh: 舊魏王肅奏祀天地，設宮懸之樂，八佾之舞，爾後因循不革。

translations.literal: Formerly Wei Wang Su memorialized on sacrificing to Heaven and Earth, establishing suspended palace music and eight-rows dance; thereafter this was followed without reform.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Wang Su of Wei memorialized on sacrifices to Heaven and Earth and established suspended palace music and the eight-rows dance. Thereafter court followed his precedent without change.

sentences.zh: 至梁武帝以為事人禮縟，事神禮簡，古無宮懸之文。

translations.literal: When Liang Emperor Wu held that rites for serving men were elaborate while rites for serving spirits were simple, antiquity had no text for suspended palace music.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang held that rites for serving men were elaborate while rites for serving spirits were simple, and that antiquity contained no precedent for suspended palace music.

sentences.zh: 陳初承用，莫有損益。

translations.literal: At Chen's beginning this was adopted and used; none added or subtracted.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Chen this practice was adopted unchanged.

sentences.zh: 宣帝欲設備樂，付有司立議，以梁武為非。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan wished to establish complete music and entrusted the relevant offices to frame discussion, holding Liang Wu in error.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan wished to establish full court music and ordered the relevant offices to debate the matter, holding Emperor Wu of Liang to have been wrong.

sentences.zh: 時碩學名儒，朝端在位，咸希旨注同。

translations.literal: At the time eminent scholars and famous Confucians at court in office all followed the imperial intent and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time eminent scholars and leading officials at court all followed the imperial intent and agreed.

sentences.zh: 察乃博引經籍，獨違群議，據梁樂為是。

translations.literal: Cha then broadly cited the classics, alone defying the collective opinion, maintaining that Liang music was correct.
translations.idiomatic: Cha then cited the classics broadly, alone defying the collective opinion and maintaining that Liang music was correct.

sentences.zh: 當時驚駭，莫不慚服。

translations.literal: At the time all were startled; none failed to feel ashamed and yield.
translations.idiomatic: All were astonished and none failed to yield in shame.

sentences.zh: 僕射徐陵因改同察議。

translations.literal: Vice Director Xu Ling thereupon changed to agree with Cha's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Xu Ling thereupon changed his view to agree with Cha.

sentences.zh: 其不順時隨俗，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His not following the times and going with custom were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His refusal to follow fashion and custom was always of this kind.

sentences.zh: 後曆仁威淮南王、平南建安王二府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as Staff Adviser in the establishments of the Prince of Huainan, Benevolent in Might, and the Prince of Jian'an, Pacifier of the South.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served in turn as Staff Adviser to the Prince of Huainan, Benevolent in Might, and the Prince of Jian'an, Pacifier of the South.

sentences.zh: 丁內憂去職。

translations.literal: He entered inner mourning and left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 俄起為戎昭將軍，知撰梁史。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as General of Martial Illumination with charge of compiling Liang history.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as General of Martial Illumination with charge of compiling the history of Liang.

sentences.zh: 後主立，兼東宮通事舍人，知撰史。

translations.literal: When the Later Sovereign was established, he was additionally Eastern Palace Communications Attendant with charge of compiling history.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Sovereign succeeded, he was additionally made Eastern Palace Communications Attendant with charge of compiling history.

sentences.zh: 至德元年，除中書侍郎，轉太子僕，余並如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, transferred to Crown Prince Vice Director, other duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhide he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and transferred to Crown Prince Vice Director while retaining his other duties.

sentences.zh: 初，梁室淪沒，察父僧垣入長安，察蔬食布衣，不聽音樂，至是凶問因聘使到江南。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Liang house was lost, Cha's father Sengyuan entered Chang'an; Cha ate vegetables and wore plain cloth, did not listen to music; now the news of death arrived in Jiangnan through the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Liang fell, Cha's father Sengyuan had gone to Chang'an. Cha ate only vegetables, wore plain cloth, and refused music. Now word of his father's death arrived in the south through an envoy.

sentences.zh: 時察母韋氏喪制適除，後主以察羸瘠，慮加毀頓，乃密遣中書舍人司馬申就宅發哀，仍敕申專加譬抑。

translations.literal: At the time Cha's mother Lady Wei had just completed her mourning term; the Later Sovereign, seeing Cha emaciated and fearing further collapse from grief, secretly sent Secretariat Drafter Sima Shen to his house to initiate mourning, and also ordered Shen specially to add counsel and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Cha's mother Lady Wei had just completed her mourning term. The Later Sovereign, seeing Cha emaciated and fearing he would ruin his health with fresh grief, secretly sent Secretariat Drafter Sima Shen to his house to initiate mourning for his father and ordered Shen to counsel and restrain him.

sentences.zh: 尋以忠毅將軍起兼東宮通事舍人，察頻讓不許。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as General of Loyal Valor with concurrent duty as Eastern Palace Communications Attendant; Cha repeatedly declined but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as General of Loyal Valor with concurrent duty as Eastern Palace Communications Attendant. Cha declined repeatedly, but the throne would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 俄敕知著作郎事。

translations.literal: Shortly an edict ordered him to oversee the Author's office.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward an edict put him in charge of the Author's office.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除給事黃門侍郎，領著作。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was made Yellow Gate Attendant-in-Ordinary with charge of authorship.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was made Yellow Gate Attendant-in-Ordinary with charge of authorship.

sentences.zh: 察既累居憂戚，齋素日久，因加氣疾。

translations.literal: Cha, having repeatedly dwelt in grief, had eaten plain food for a long time and thereby contracted a qi disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Cha had lived long in grief and eaten plain food for many years, and he contracted a disorder of the vital breath.

sentences.zh: 後主嘗別召見，為之動容，命停長齋，令從晚食。

translations.literal: The Later Sovereign once summoned him separately; moved on his account, he ordered an end to prolonged fasting and allowed evening meals.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Sovereign once summoned him privately, was moved by his condition, ordered an end to prolonged fasting, and allowed him evening meals.

sentences.zh: 又詔授秘書監，領著作，奏撰中書表集。

translations.literal: Again by edict he was made Director of the Secretariat with charge of authorship and memorialized to compile the Secretariat Memorial Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Director of the Secretariat with charge of authorship and ordered to compile the Secretariat Memorial Collection.

sentences.zh: 曆度支、吏部二尚書。

translations.literal: He successively served as Minister of Revenue and Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Minister of Revenue and Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 察自居顯要，一不交通。

translations.literal: Once Cha held a prominent post, he had no dealings whatsoever.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held high office, Cha kept no private dealings with anyone.

sentences.zh: 嘗有私門生不敢厚餉，送南布一端，花綀一匹。

translations.literal: Once a private student, not daring a lavish gift, sent one bolt of southern cloth and one piece of figured silk.
translations.idiomatic: Once a private student, not daring a lavish gift, sent one bolt of southern cloth and one piece of figured silk.

sentences.zh: 察謂曰：「吾所衣著，止是麻布蒲綀，此物於吾無用。

translations.literal: Cha said: "What I wear is only hemp cloth and rush silk—these things are useless to me.
translations.idiomatic: Cha said, "I wear only hemp cloth and rush silk. These things are useless to me.

sentences.zh: 既欲相款接，幸不煩爾。」

translations.literal: Since you wish to treat me warmly, I hope you will not trouble yourself thus."
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to be friendly with me, please do not trouble yourself with such gifts."

sentences.zh: 此人遜請，察厲色驅出，自是莫敢饋遺。

translations.literal: The man humbly pleaded; Cha with stern countenance drove him out—from then on none dared offer gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The man pleaded humbly, but Cha drove him out with a stern face. From then on no one dared offer him gifts.

sentences.zh: 陳亡入隋，詔授秘書丞，別敕成梁、陳二史。

translations.literal: When Chen perished and he entered Sui, by edict he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, with separate command to complete the histories of Liang and Chen.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell and he entered the Sui, he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat by edict, with a separate order to complete the histories of Liang and Chen.

sentences.zh: 又敕于朱華閣長參。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to attend long at the Vermilion Flower Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to attend regularly at the Vermilion Flower Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 文帝知察蔬菲，別日獨召入內殿，賜果菜，指謂朝臣曰：「聞姚察學行當今無比，我平陳唯得此一人。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen knew Cha ate vegetables sparingly; on a separate day he summoned him alone into the inner hall, bestowed fruits and vegetables, pointed and told the court ministers: "I hear Yao Cha's learning and conduct are unmatched today—in pacifying Chen I gained only this one man."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen knew Cha lived frugally on vegetables. On another day he summoned him alone to the inner hall, gave him fruits and vegetables, and told the court ministers, "I hear Yao Cha's learning and conduct are unmatched today. In pacifying Chen I gained only this one man."

sentences.zh: 開皇十三年，襲封北絳郡公。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kaihuang he inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Northern Jiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Kaihuang he inherited the title Duke of Northern Jiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 察在陳時聘周，因得與父僧垣相見，將別之際，絕而復蘇。

translations.literal: When Cha was on mission to Zhou under Chen, he was able to see his father Sengyuan; at the moment of parting he fainted and revived.
translations.idiomatic: While serving Chen on a mission to Zhou, Cha was able to see his father Sengyuan. At their parting he fainted and revived.

sentences.zh: 至是承襲，愈更悲感，見者莫不為之歔欷。

translations.literal: Now inheriting the title, his grief grew still deeper; all who saw could not but sigh for him.
translations.idiomatic: Now, on inheriting his father's title, his grief deepened still further, and all who saw him sighed.

sentences.zh: 丁後母杜氏喪，解職。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his stepmother Lady Du and left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his stepmother Lady Du.

sentences.zh: 在服制之中，有白鳩巢於戶上。

translations.literal: While in mourning garb, a white turtledove nested above his door.
translations.idiomatic: While he was in mourning, a white turtledove nested above his door.

sentences.zh: 仁壽二年，詔除員外散騎常侍、晉王侍讀。

translations.literal: In the second year of Renshou, by edict he was made Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Reader to the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Renshou, an edict appointed him Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and reader to the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，授太子內舍人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he was appointed Inner Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he was appointed Inner Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 及改易衣冠，刪定朝式，預參對問。

translations.literal: When dress and caps were changed and court ceremonial was revised, he took part in close questioning and answers.
translations.idiomatic: When court dress was changed and court ritual revised, he took part in close questioning and direct answers.

sentences.zh: 大業二年，終於東都。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daye he died in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daye he died in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 遺命薄葬，以松板薄棺，才可容身，土周於棺而已。

translations.literal: His testament ordered a plain burial: pine boards and a thin coffin barely large enough for the body, with earth only around the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: His testament ordered a plain burial: pine boards and a thin coffin barely large enough for the body, with earth only around the coffin.

sentences.zh: 葬日，止麤車即送厝舊塋北。

translations.literal: On the burial day only a rough cart was used, and he was sent to be laid beside the old tomb to the north.
translations.idiomatic: On the burial day only a rough cart was used, and he was sent to be laid beside the old tomb to the north.

sentences.zh: 不須立靈，置一小床，每日設清水，六齋日設齋食菜果，任家有無，不須別經營也。

translations.literal: Do not set up a spirit tablet; place a small bed and daily set out clear water. On the six fast days set out vegetarian food, vegetables, and fruit—as the household can afford, without special arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: Do not set up a spirit tablet. Place a small bed and each day set out clear water. On the six fast days set out vegetarian food, vegetables, and fruit—as the household can afford, without special arrangements.

sentences.zh: 初，察欲讀一藏經，並已究竟，將終，曾無痛惱，但西向坐正念，云：「一切空寂」。

translations.literal: Earlier Cha had wished to read the full canon of scriptures and had already mastered it; nearing the end he felt no pain or distress, only sat facing west in right mindfulness, saying: "All is empty and still."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Cha had wished to read the full Buddhist canon and had already mastered it. Near the end he felt no pain, only sat facing west in meditation, saying, "All is empty and still."

sentences.zh: 其後身體柔軟，顏色如恒。

translations.literal: Afterward his body was soft and supple, his complexion as in ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward his body remained soft and his complexion unchanged.

sentences.zh: 兩宮悼惜，贈賵甚厚。

translations.literal: Both palaces mourned him; funeral gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Both palaces mourned him and sent lavish funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 察至孝，有人倫鑒識，沖虛謙遜，不以所長矜人。

translations.literal: Cha was utmost in filial piety, had discernment in human relations, was mild, empty, and humble, and did not flaunt his strengths before others.
translations.idiomatic: Cha was deeply filial, discerning in human relations, gentle and humble, and never flaunted his strengths before others.

sentences.zh: 專志著書，白首不倦。

translations.literal: He devoted his will to writing books, white-haired yet never weary.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to writing and never tired even in old age.

sentences.zh: 所著漢書訓纂三十卷，說林十卷，西聘、玉璽、建康三鍾等記各一卷，文集二十卷。

translations.literal: Works he composed: Exegesis and Compilation of the Book of Han in thirty juan, Forest of Discourse in ten juan, records of the Western Mission, the Jade Seal, and the Three Bells of Jiankang, each one juan, and a literary collection in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His works included Exegesis and Compilation of the Book of Han in thirty juan, Forest of Discourse in ten juan, records of the Western Mission, the Jade Seal, and the Three Bells of Jiankang, each in one juan, and a literary collection of twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 所撰梁、陳史，雖未畢功，隋開皇中，文帝遣中書舍人虞世基索本，且進。

translations.literal: The Liang and Chen histories he composed, though not finished, in Sui's Kaihuang era Emperor Wen sent Secretariat Drafter Yu Shiji to request the manuscript and have it submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The histories of Liang and Chen he composed were unfinished, but in the Kaihuang era Emperor Wen sent Secretariat Drafter Yu Shiji to request the manuscript and have it submitted.

sentences.zh: 臨亡，戒子思廉撰續。

translations.literal: Facing death, he admonished his son Silian to compile and continue them.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he charged his son Silian to continue the work.

sentences.zh: 思廉在陳為衡陽王府法曹參軍、會稽王主簿。

translations.literal: Silian under Chen was Legal Section Assistant in the Prince of Hengyang's establishment and Chief Clerk to the Prince of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chen, Silian had served as Legal Section Assistant in the establishment of the Prince of Hengyang and as Chief Clerk to the Prince of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 論曰：沈炯才思之美，足以繼踵前良。

translations.literal: The judgment says: Shen Jiong's beauty of talent and thought was enough to follow in the footsteps of former worthies.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Shen Jiong's literary gifts were fine enough to follow in the footsteps of former masters.

sentences.zh: 然仕于梁朝，年已知命，主非不文，而位裁邑宰。

translations.literal: Yet serving in the Liang court, his years already knew Heaven's command; his lord was not without culture, yet his post was only that of district magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet under the Liang he had already reached the age of fifty. His sovereign was not uncultured, yet Jiong rose no higher than district magistrate.

sentences.zh: 及於運逢交喪，驅馳戎馬，所在稱美，用舍信有時焉。

translations.literal: When fate met overlapping calamity and he drove through war-horses, wherever he went he won praise—employment and dismissal truly have their seasons.
translations.idiomatic: When turmoil overtook the realm and he rode through war, he won praise wherever he went. Use and dismissal truly have their seasons.

sentences.zh: 虞荔弟兄，才行兼著，崎嶇喪亂，保茲貞一，並取貴時主，豈虛得乎。

translations.literal: Yu Li and his brothers were outstanding in conduct and talent; through rugged ruin and disorder they preserved this single integrity, and both won honor from the sovereigns of their age—was it gained in vain?
translations.idiomatic: Yu Li and his brothers were outstanding in talent and conduct. Through ruin and disorder they preserved their integrity and won honor from their sovereigns. They earned it fairly.

sentences.zh: 傅縡聰警特達，才氣自負，行之平日，其猶殆諸；

translations.literal: Fu Zai was clever, alert, and outstanding; he relied on his own talent and spirit—in ordinary conduct it was already perilous;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zai was brilliant and outstanding, arrogant in his gifts. In ordinary times his conduct was already perilous;

sentences.zh: 處以危邦，死其宜矣。

translations.literal: placed in a perilous state, to die was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: placed in a doomed state, his death was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 顧、姚棲托藝文，蹈履清直，文質彬彬，各踐通賢之域，美矣乎！

translations.literal: Gu and Yao lodged in literary arts, trod the path of pure uprightness, wen and substance balanced and refined, each entering the realm of penetrating worthies—how beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: Gu and Yao devoted themselves to letters, walked the path of pure integrity, and balanced substance with style. Each reached the realm of true excellence. How admirable!
